films.title: Ma nuit chez maud (My Night at Maud's)
intro: By the late 1960s, free love, ‘God is dead’ slogans and psychedelic colours were all the rage. It was during this very period that Rohmer made this masterful black-and-white dialogue-driven film about love, faith and moral doubt, in which philosophical conversations culminate in a subtle interplay of seduction and desire. Ma nuit chez Maud is an absolute masterpiece.
description: During the turbulent year of 1968, Rohmer shot Ma nuit chez Maud far removed from the Paris May revolt. Set in wintry Clermont-Ferrand, Nestor Almendros’s stunning black-and-white cinematography creates a world of snow, cold and cosy interiors. The film is regarded as Rohmer’s first – and perhaps his absolute – masterpiece and one of cinema’s great ‘talking films’. The Catholic engineer Jean-Louis is torn between the free-spirited, intellectual Maud and the angelic young Christine, whom he sees as his future wife after just one encounter. Long conversations about Pascal, free will, faith, chance and seduction form the core of the film, in which words and body language constantly contradict one another. Rohmer suggests how the erotic and the spiritual are inextricably intertwined. Thanks to the subtle direction and the brilliant performances by Jean-Louis Trintignant and Françoise Fabian, Ma nuit chez Maud offers an ideal introduction to his unique cinematic world.

imdb.title: My Night at Maud's

films.title: Minotaur
intro: After an almost decade-long absence, Russian filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev returns with Minotaur, a visually stunning masterpiece inspired by Claude Chabrol’s La Femme infidèle. Set in an unnamed Russian city, the film follows businessman Gleb, who is ordered to hand over fourteen employees for the war against Ukraine while confronting his wife’s affair. What begins as a tense marital thriller gradually reveals the pervasive impact of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine on everyday life. Rich in references to the Greek Minotaur myth, the film combines personal drama with sharp social observation. Enhanced by an evocative score from Evgueni and Sacha Galperine, Minotaur confirms Zvyagintsev’s status as one of contemporary cinema's great auteurs.
description: Zvyagintsev shows how major social developments intrude on everyday life, without ever reducing his characters to mere symbols.

films.title: Nadja
intro: A dreamy arthouse vampire film from the early nineties—produced by David Lynch—receives a brand-new live score by ambient pop's rising star, more eaze.Drawing inspiration from Dracula's Daughter (1936) and André Breton's surrealist novel Nadja (1928), director Michael Almereyda's acclaimed cult film follows the enigmatic vampire Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) as she returns to New York City to avenge her father Dracula's death at the hands of Dr. Van Helsing, played by sixties screen icon Peter Fonda.
description: After Dracula's death—represented by a repurposed shot of Bela Lugosi from the 1932 film White Zombie—Nadja arrives at a Manhattan morgue to collect his body. She slips effortlessly into the city's nocturnal hipster scene, spending her nights drinking coffee, smoking cigarettes, wandering downtown bars, and engaging in deadpan philosophical conversations. Meanwhile, the eccentric Dr. Van Helsing relentlessly pursues Dracula's daughter through the streets of New York.Visually, Nadja is as distinctive as its story. Almereyda combines luminous black-and-white 35mm cinematography with haunting Pixelvision footage shot on a Fisher-Price toy camera, creating a dreamlike, low-fi aesthetic unlike anything else. More interested in atmosphere than conventional horror, the film replaces gore and jump scares with melancholy, emotional unease, dry humour, and a hypnotic sense of mystery. It is as much a portrait of early 1990s downtown New York as it is a vampire film, evoking the worlds of Jim Jarmusch, Hal Hartley, and David Lynch.Equally difficult to categorize is more eaze, the project of Brooklyn-based sound artist and multi-instrumentalist Mari Maurice. Blending ambient pop, folk, musique concrète, and experimental electronics, Maurice transforms everyday sounds and acoustic instrumentation into richly textured, emotionally resonant compositions. Exploring themes of intimacy, longing, memory, and transformation, more eaze has become one of the most exciting voices in contemporary experimental music, with releases on Thrill Jockey, Leaving Records, Longform Editions, Ecstatic, Orange Milk, and 15 Love. As a string arranger, pedal steel player, and producer, Maurice has also collaborated with artists including Claire Rousay, Lomelda, Space Afrika, Martha Skye Murphy, Water Damage, Fashion Club, Rainy Miller, and Nick Zanca.
For Videodroom, more eaze brings a new musical interpretation to this haunting cult classic, creating a unique encounter between adventurous cinema and contemporary experimental sound.

imdb.plot: A vampire family deals with their father's death in NYC while being pursued by Van Helsing and his nephew. Love and destruction clash in this modern vampire story.

films.title: Pauline à la plage (Pauline at the Beach)
intro: Rohmer’s third instalment in the Comédies et proverbes cycle is a nuanced, sultry, summery film. It is an erotic comedy, thought through down to the finest detail, about six young people who find themselves caught up in a web of love and desire. At a holiday resort on the Normandy coast, the adults lose themselves in temptation, misunderstandings and self-deception.
description: The third instalment of Comédies et proverbes (Comedies and Proverbs) is a delightful summer comedy of manners about love, lust and misunderstandings. In a seaside resort on the Normandy coast, six characters become entangled in a web of flirtation, jealousy and poor choices. Fifteen-year-old Pauline (Amanda Langlet) observes with an innocent eye as the adults lose themselves in theories about love, whilst their amorous schemes rarely yield the desired result. What begins as a charming vaudeville gradually takes on a melancholic undertone. Rohmer combines sophisticated dialogue with a seemingly simple yet extremely precise mise-en-scène. The sunny beaches, the gentle September light and the subtle colour compositions inspired by Matisse make Pauline à la plage one of his most sensual and visually enchanting films, thanks also to the understated virtuosity of master cinematographer Nestor Almendros.

films.title: The Six
intro: In the early 1980s, six graduates from Antwerp’s fashion academy transformed the city into an international fashion hub. Known as The Antwerp Six, they became a global phenomenon despite their very different styles. In The Six, filmmaker Reiner Holzemer explores their shared history and the origins of their legendary collective identity.
description: Between 1980 and 1982, six students graduated from the fashion department of the Royal Academy of Fine Arts in Antwerp who would go on to radically change the image of fashion and elevate Antwerp to the status of a fashion city. Walter Van Beirendonck, Ann Demeulemeester, Dries Van Noten, Dirk Van Saene, Marina Yee and Dirk Bikkembergs are six very different designers. But 40 years ago they were launched internationally as The Antwerp Six and quickly took on a near-mythical status in the international fashion world. German documentary maker Reiner Holzemer, who has made films about photographers such as Anton Corbijn and Juergen Teller, previously portrayed Van Noten in Dries. With The Six, he delves into the history of The Antwerp Six. Was that group identity genuine, or mainly a construct of the outside world? Holzemer explores this through their personal stories, with a wonderful soundtrack by Antwerp band Dez Mona.

films.title: Variations on a Theme
intro: Hope keeps one going, but it can also hold captive. In the South African docu-fiction hybrid Variations on a Theme, nearly eighty-year-old Hettie is still waiting for compensation for her father's military service, despite being lied to time and again. Who can blame her for continuing to dream? Directors Jason Jacobs and Devon Delmar, recognised as rising talents at the International Film Festival Rotterdam, paint a serene portrait, rooted in the landscape and local community. Recurring imagery gently recounts its own, unfinished story, full of bittersweet poetry. As the South African-raised crooner Al Bowlly sings during the closing credits: “Dreaming the lonely night through.”
description: Deliberately still and contemplative, their poetic docufiction bears witness to a sad, haunting beauty.

films.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
intro: In 1972, filmmaker William Greaves gathered artists, writers and musicians associated with the Harlem Renaissance at Duke Ellington’s home for a historic four-hour meeting. Half a century later, his son David transformed the footage into Once Upon a Time in Harlem, an intimate documentary that brings this extraordinary cultural encounter vividly back to life.
description: In 1972, the African-American filmmaker William Greaves brought together an exceptional group of people. All the guests were associated with the Harlem Renaissance, a period of cultural and intellectual flourishing in the 1920s. From Harlem, African-American artists, writers and musicians forged a new sense of self-awareness and a voice of their own that would permanently transform American culture. Names such as Romare Bearden, Eubie Blake and James Van Der Zee may have been forgotten, but their influence endures. Using four cameras, Greaves filmed the four-hour reunion. Fifty years later, Greaves’ son David has condensed this legendary gathering into the documentary Once Upon a Time in Harlem. The result is a sublime talk film in which vivid memories and anecdotes are brought to life, creating a fascinating snapshot of the era. At the same time, it is a moving tribute to the achievements of these extraordinary artists and their legacy.

films.title: The Loneliest Man in Town
intro: As his Vienna apartment filled with musical memorabilia faces demolition, ageing bluesman Al Cook finds himself surrounded by memories of a life lived to the rhythm of Elvis and the blues. Tizza Covi and Rainer Frimmel blur fact and fiction in this tender, wry portrait of a man forced to let go, and finally chase a long-deferred dream.
description: The Austrian blues musician and die-hard Elvis fan Al Cook often has the same nightmare: he is playing a piano from which the black keys have vanished. In his real life, too, more and more is at risk of disappearing: his glory days are behind him, his wife has passed away, Vienna no longer feels like home, and soon his flat, full of memories and musical memorabilia, is due to be demolished. Now that the world seems to be moving on without him, it is time for a radical new beginning. The directing duo Tizza Covi and Rainer Frimmel, known for their boundary-blurring cinema that straddles fiction and reality, have their friend and real-life artist Al Cook play a version of himself: an amiable man possessed by nostalgia. With plenty of melancholy and dry humour, the result is a minimalist portrait of a headstrong older man in his twilight years. Rich in its simplicity and grand in its sensitivity, The Loneliest Man in Town could rank amongst the finest works of Aki Kaurismäki.

films.title: No Good Men
intro: A feelgood film in a feel bad place, is the tagline for No Good Men, which opened this year’s Berlin International Film Festival. It serves a flesh-and-blood love story in Afghanistan on the eve of the Taliban’s return to power. Screenwriter, director, and lead actress Shahrbanoo Sadat takes a critical look back at what were said to be the last days of freedom for Afghan women in 2021. As with Wolf and Sheep (2016) and The Orphanage (2019), the Iranian-born Afghan filmmaker draws inspiration from the unpublished diaries of Anwar Hashimi, her co-star. The two met years ago when they worked for the same TV station in Kabul. A deliberate rosy piece of fiction with deep red roots in reality.
description: A political romantic comedy that isn't afraid to shift in tone.

films.title: Tegenwoordig heet iedereen Sorry (9+) (Everyone’s Sorry Nowadays)
intro: On a sweltering summer day, almost 13-year-old Bianca finds an unlikely confidante in her idol Billie King, a soap star who suddenly appears on her sofa. Frederike Migom, whose previous film Binti (2019) won the Ensor for Best Youth Film, turns Bart Moeyaert's beloved novel into a sun-drenched reverie on growing up, feeling invisible and the aching desire to be truly seen.
description: Bianca is a strong-willed girl of almost thirteen. She's not an easy child, according to her mother; “unmanageable”, according to her father and his new girlfriend, Cruz. Meanwhile, her little brother Alan, who needs constant care, hogs all the attention, making Bianca feel invisible. Until, one sweltering summer’s day, her great idol Billie King, a soap opera actress, suddenly turns up in the living room. Their unexpected conversations put into words feelings she cannot share with anyone else and teach her that she is, in fact, quite great. Following the award-winning Binti, which won the Ensor for Best Youth Film, Frederike Migom adapts Bart Moeyaerts’s much-loved book into a playful, moving film about the whimsical inner world of a teenager and the longing to be seen. With tenderness, humour and a dash of fantasy, she captures one chaotic day in the life of Bianca, a girl who, above all, wants to find her own place in the world.

films.title: The Mad Dog of Europe
intro: Long before the world grasped the scale of the threat, screenwriter Herman Mankiewicz tried to expose Hitler through cinema. This documentary follows the fate of that abandoned production, revealing political pressure, studio hesitation and prejudice in Hollywood through vivid archives and insightful interviews. A tale of courage and silence unseen.
description: Six years ago, David Fincher tried to rescue Herman Mankiewicz from the obscurity of classic Hollywood with the biopic Mank. The man won an Oscar, among other things, as co-writer of Citizen Kane. In 1933 — by which time he already had dozens of screenwriting credits to his name — he tried to warn the world about the rise of Adolf Hitler with The Mad Dog of Europe. Hitler himself believed cinema was the ideal means of winning the masses over to his side, and Mankiewicz wanted to attack him with his own weapons. But no studio wanted to burn its fingers on the script. Rumour had it that if the film were made, Nazi Germany would ban all American titles from its cinemas. Through interviews and fascinating archive footage, the documentary The Mad Dog of Europe tells the story of this doomed film, and paints a picture of the antisemitism Mankiewicz had to endure, including in Hollywood.

films.title: Les nuits de la pleine lune (Full Moon in Paris)
intro: In Full Moon in Paris, we see how Louise tries to reconcile her longing for freedom and love, but gradually becomes entangled in her own contradictions. This witty and melancholic romantic comedy features one of Rohmer’s most memorable heroines and, with its sophisticated visual language, is also one of his most formalist works.
description: The fourth instalment of Comédies et proverbes features one of the most memorable heroines in Rohmer’s work: Louise, a young designer who yearns for both love and independence and perhaps expects too much from life. She temporarily leaves her boyfriend Rémi to live alone in Paris once more, convinced that she can combine freedom with a relationship. With humour and compassion, Rohmer shows how her dreams clash with reality. Architecture and interiors beautifully reflect the inner worlds of his characters. With its symmetrical compositions and sophisticated colour schemes, this is also one of his most formalist films. Pascale Ogier’s spontaneous, melancholic performance lends the film a special intensity, to which the evocation of Parisian nightlife in the early 1980s also contributes. Following Ogier’s tragic death shortly after filming, the film also became one of Rohmer’s most moving works.

Determined to save the celebration, Shaun experiments with daring fixes that soon spiral out of control. When the Farmer disappears and a strange creature appears in the woods, Shaun must face his wildest adventure yet. Chaos reigns!
description: At Mossy Bottom Farm, where Shaun the Sheep lives, an excited atmosphere prevails, as Halloween is on its way. Unfortunately, the farmer accidentally destroys Shaun and his friends' pumpkin harvest. All the festive plans threaten to fall through, but Shaun refuses to accept defeat. With wild ideas and the confidence of a mad scientist, he tries to repair the damage. However, he fails to realise that in doing so, he's bringing an even bigger problem upon himself. The farmer has vanished, and a mysterious beast is creeping through the woods. Spooky without losing its warm charm, and mischievous without frightening off younger viewers, Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom combines successful Halloween tension, visual humour and inventive chaos. The handmade stop-motion animation gives every startled look, frantic chase and comic blunder its own unique and irresistible character.

films.title: Ombres de soie
intro: In 1930s Shanghai, the layered friendship between Lysanne and Marlène unfolds as their bond evolves over time. In her directorial debut Ombres de soie, Mary Stephen creates a sensual film essay on identity and belonging, exploring the tension between East and West while questioning fixed ideas about culture, gender and colonial legacies through a poetic feminist lens.
description: Before collaborating with Éric Rohmer as an editor, Mary Stephen made her remarkable directorial debut with Ombres de soie. Set in Shanghai in 1935, the film follows Lysanne and Marlène, two women who have known each other since their school days. As their lives unfold, their bond evolves and their relationship develops into a complex quest for identity and connection.

With her sensual imagery, fragmentary narrative structure and layered sound design, Stephen creates a poetic film essay in which memories, voices and glances enter into dialogue. Inspired by Marguerite Duras’ India Song and the writings of author Eileen Chang, she explores the tension between East and West. The film challenges dogmatic notions of ethnicity and gender and demonstrates how personal relationships are shaped by broader historical forces. The recently restored film once again reveals Stephen’s unique feminist and postcolonial perspective.

films.title: Le rayon vert (The Green Ray)
intro: In this quasi-experimental, ironic film, in which realism is occasionally infused with a touch of magic, we follow Parisian Delphine’s solitary quest for true love. As she wanders in vain through French holiday resorts, chance and self-deception ultimately lead her to a revelation.
description: In the fifth instalment of Comédies et proverbes, Rohmer boldly blends realism and magic. We follow Delphine (Marie Rivière), a young, shy Parisienne who, following a break-up, travels aimlessly through French holiday resorts. Unlike Rohmer’s usual ensemble pieces, this film revolves entirely around Delphine’s search for true love and her refusal to settle for superficial relationships. The title refers to the rare green light at sunset, which, according to Jules Verne, offers insight into one’s feelings. Rohmer builds slowly towards this symbolic moment in a film that was largely improvised and adopts an exceptionally documentary-like style. The tension arises from the contrast between the sunny holiday world, Delphine’s inner crisis and the enchanting moment of epiphany. Awarded the Golden Lion in Venice, Le Rayon vert went on to become one of Rohmer’s most beloved and personal films.

films.title: L'amour l’après-midi (Love in the Afternoon)
intro: In L’amour l’après-midi, Rohmer presents us with a virtuous protagonist, Frédéric, who is determined not to succumb to the temptations of promiscuity. However, when he meets Chloé, that resolve is put under strain. This film is a thoughtful, moral love story about a happily married bourgeois man and the woman who tests his desires and his fidelity.
description: Upon its release, the final instalment of the Contes moraux received a lukewarm reception, but L’amour l’après-midi is now regarded as one of Rohmer’s finest works. Whilst the sexual revolution was in full swing, Rohmer chose a protagonist who tries to resist temptation. The married Frédéric (Bernard Verley as the director’s stand-in?) leads a quiet, bourgeois life, but harbours romantic fantasies which Rohmer playfully depicts in an anthology scene in which the actresses from earlier Contes moraux appear on the streets of Paris. However, Frédéric’s equilibrium and marital fidelity are disrupted when the promiscuous Chloé (Zouzou) reappears in his life. Thanks to the natural performances, the astute psychological observations and the meticulous evocation of early 1970s Paris, the film has become one of Rohmer’s most nuanced and profound studies of the trials and tribulations of love.

films.title: Un bon petit soldat
intro: In Un bon petit soldat, Stéphane Brizé returns to one of his favourite battlegrounds: the modern workplace. Alba Rohrwacher is superb as Carla, the newly appointed HR manager of a major insurance company, tasked with reconciling employee wellbeing with relentless performance targets. When she uncovers a case of toxic management, her faith in the corporate playbook begins to crack. In a claustrophobic world of employer branding, happiness workshops and endless targets, Brizé dissects the human cost of a system in which even wellbeing is expected to deliver results.
description: The film is as oppressive as it is cutting: a masterpiece about work, power and precious time in a world where people have become a resource.

films.title: Le beau mariage (A Good Marriage)
intro: Rohmer remains true, in all circumstances, to the kind of film with which he made his debut in the 1960s: a subtle analysis of (falling in) love. This film is a highly charming, ironic comedy about Sabine’s obsessive quest for marriage, in which falling in love, self-deception and rational illusions are delicately dissected.
description: In the second part of Comédies et proverbes, Rohmer continues to dissect love, this time through a heroine who attempts to organise her infatuation in a rational manner. Sabine (Béatrice Romand, who was a naive girl in Le genou de Claire but is now a grown woman) impulsively decides to get married and is convinced that the lawyer Edmond (André Dussolier) will be her ideal husband, even though he shows little interest in her. Her carefully thought-out strategy results in a series of painful but often comical misunderstandings. Sabine commutes between her hometown of Le Mans and Paris, whilst chattering endlessly with her best friend (the ethereal Arielle Dombasle). Rohmer approaches her with a blend of irony and empathy: he does not judge her, but shows how dreams and self-deception go hand in hand. The film is a playful study of romantic illusions, in which the understated mise-en-scène and flawless editing dissect the characters’ psychology with exquisite precision.

imdb.plot: Sabine vows to give up married lovers, and is determined to find a good husband. Her best friend Clarisse introduces her to her cousin Edmond, a busy lawyer from Paris. Sabine pursues Edmond, with the encouragement of Clarisse, but Edmond does not seem very interested.

films.title: La carrière de Suzanne (Suzanne's Career)
intro: La carrière de Suzanne (Suzanne's Career) is an evocative comedy about friendship, seduction and morality, in which the insecure protagonist allows himself to be swept away by a cynical womaniser. In this medium-length film, Rohmer’s artistry in laying bare the emotional truth of his characters as accurately as possible is truly evident for the first time.
description: In the medium-length film La Carrière de Suzanne (Suzanne's Career), Rohmer finds his own voice for the first time. Inspired by literature and philosophy, he reveals, without stylistic bravado, the emotional truth of his characters. The shy student Bertrand allows himself to be swept along by his cynical friend Guillaume, who seduces and exploits the sensual Suzanne. Against a backdrop of cafés and Parisian nightlife, Rohmer explores friendship, lust and moral ambiguity, already foreshadowing the psychological subtlety of his later work.

films.title: La boulangère de monceau (The Bakery Girl of Monceau)
intro: La Boulangère de Monceau is a short, playful tale of falling in love and seduction, in which a young Parisian is torn between two women but ultimately remains faithful to his first love. The themes that would later recur as central motifs in Rohmer’s body of work, are all already present here.
description: Three years after the fiasco of his ill-fated debut Le Signe du lion (1959), Rohmer shot La Boulangère de Monceau (The Bakery Girl of Monceau, 1963) using borrowed 16mm equipment; it was the first of his Six Moral Tales. A young Parisian (Barbet Schroeder) dumps a baker’s daughter as soon as the woman he is truly in love with reappears. This 22-minute short film already contains all the central themes – wandering, chance, desire and moral choice – and narrative strategies that characterise Rohmer’s later work.

films.title: Conte d’automne (Autumn Tale)
intro: The fourth and last part of Rohmer's Tales of the Four Seasons — A Tale of Autumn — is a fresh, sophisticated romantic comedy in which hidden agendas, misunderstandings and adult desires come together against the natural backdrop of the Rhône Valley wine region.
description: In the fourth and final instalment of Tales of the Four Seasons, Rohmer – then aged 78 – turns his attention to the romantic entanglements of adults. The heroine, Magali (Béatrice Romand), is a 45-year-old widow and winegrower who is left alone in the Ardèche after her children have moved away. She longs for a new love, but is reluctant to take the initiative herself. Two friends therefore decide to secretly find her a partner, leading to misunderstandings and unexpected complications. Rohmer does not turn this simple premise into a classic vaudeville, but rather into a refined marivaudage full of irony, subtle humour and moral observation. His characters discover that people rarely act as they predict. As always, he links the mundane with the romantic: great emotions unfold in everyday circumstances. Rohmer captures the autumnal landscapes of the Rhône Valley with his characteristic precision.

films.title: La Collectionneuse (The Collector)
intro: The Contes moraux follow a similar narrative pattern: a man who is already committed to a woman finds himself drawn to a second woman, leading to a moral crisis. The light-hearted, ironic La collectionneuse fits perfectly into this tradition and depicts temptation, jealousy and moral self-control, in which psychological games probe the boundaries between lust and self-deception.
description: La Collectionneuse, Rohmer’s third filmed but officially fourth Contes Moraux, marked the breakthrough of his first cycle to a wider cinephile audience. As in all the Contes Moraux, a man is seduced by a second woman, but ultimately returns to his first love. In a villa near Saint-Tropez (the city of all sins ever since the Vadim-Bardot duo shot Et Dieu créa la femme there), Adrien, Daniel and Haydée share sultry summer days. Haydée, the ‘collector’ of the title, constantly switches lovers, whilst Adrien and Daniel believe they can manipulate her. Their psychological games result in misunderstandings and ironic defeats. The sunny, sensual atmosphere makes this variation on Rohmer’s ethical and emotional themes deceptively light-hearted, for the film also leaves a bitter aftertaste. During rehearsals, Rohmer allowed the actors to help shape their dialogue, which lends this amorous round dance a striking spontaneity.

imdb.title: The Collector

films.title: Conte d’été (A Summer's Tale)
intro: In this enchanting, summery Rohmer film, the indecisive musician Gaspard must choose between three women. Although he tries to make a rational choice, it is ultimately love, chance and self-discovery that set the tone in Conte d’été. The natural performances and the light-hearted atmosphere of the Normandy coast create a sparkling lightness in the film.
description: The subtly crafted third instalment of Rohmer’s Contes des quatre saisons is a refined summer romantic comedy about doubt, desire and indecision, and one of Rohmer’s few films featuring a male protagonist. Whilst on holiday in Dinard, the young musician Gaspard (Melvil Poupaud) waits for his beloved Léna, but in the meantime becomes entangled in a subtle game with the outspoken Margot (Amanda Langlet) and the sensual Solène (Gwenaëlle Simon). Gaspard tries to make a rational choice, but is characterised above all by hesitation. Rohmer paints a sensitive portrait of this anti-hero as someone who does not know himself well and prefers to let reality decide. The natural performances and the summery, sensual atmosphere of the Normandy coast lend the film a sparkling lightness. With long walks by the sea, music and chance encounters, Rohmer once again demonstrates how the everyday can be transformed into pure cinema.

imdb.title: A Summer's Tale
imdb.plot: As a reserved young graduate vacations in a seaside town, he hopes his girlfriend will join him. But he ends up bonding with a local young woman whose female friend is also smitten with him.

films.title: Conte d’hiver (A Tale of Winter)
intro: Due to a misunderstanding, Félicie loses all trace of Charles, her great holiday romance. She however is convinced that she will find him again one day. In this thoughtful, melancholic romance, an unwavering belief in love, the wonder of unexpected chance and fate create a tension that drives the film’s narrative.
description: In Conte d’hiver, shot in austere 16mm footage and set against grey suburban backdrops, Rohmer explores the power of chance, loyalty and faith. Five years after hairdresser Félicie (a moving performance by Charlotte Véry) lost contact with her holiday romance, Charles, due to a mistake, she remains convinced that she will find him again one day. Meanwhile, she refuses to commit to two men – another hairdresser and a librarian – who offer her security, but not true love. Inspired by Shakespeare’s The Winter’s Tale, Rohmer weaves a seemingly everyday story with an almost fairy-tale-like belief in the improbable. A visit to Nevers cathedral and a revelation whilst attending a Shakespeare performance reinforce the spiritual dimension of Félicie’s quest. Philosophical discussions about Pascal and Plato contrast with Félicie’s intuitive trust in fate.

imdb.title: A Tale of Winter

films.title: Conte de printemps (A Tale of Springtime)
intro: The first instalment in the Contes des quatre saisons (Tales of the Four Seasons) cycle is a gently ironic film about love, truth and philosophical doubt, in which Rohmer affectionately mocks intellectuals and their need to explain everything.
description: In the first film of the Contes des quatre saisons (Tales of the Four Seasons) cycle, spring not only provides the backdrop but also subtly influences the characters’ behaviour. Philosophy lecturer Jeanne (Anne Teyssèdre), inspired by Kant, befriends the young pianist Natacha, who seems keen to set her up with her father, Igor. A playful web of misunderstandings, mistrust and romantic intrigues unravels around a missing necklace. Rohmer weaves philosophical ideas about truth and knowledge into a light-hearted marivaudage, in which the characters endlessly reflect on their feelings. With gentle irony, he portrays an intellectual milieu without mocking it. With inspired conversations, music by Schumann and Beethoven, and set against the backdrop of a spacious Parisian flat and country homes in Fontainebleau, Conte de printemps is supremely refined and a pure delight to listen to and watch.

imdb.title: A Tale of Springtime
imdb.plot: Simple conversations engender complicated human interactions. Jeanne is open and even-tempered, a philosophy teacher at a lycée. Her fiancé is away and she doesn't want to stay at his messy flat; she's loaned hers to a cousin, so she accepts the invitation of Natasha, a music student whom she meets at a party, to sleep in her father Igor's bedroom because he's always with his young girlfriend, Eve. Natasha tells Jeanne a story of a missing necklace and her suspicions of Eve. They all meet at dinner, then again at Igor's country house. Is Natasha scheming to get Igor and Jeanne together alone? Once alone, what determines how they choose to act? And the necklace, what of it?

films.title: DAO
intro: “Families can be complicated,” is heard at the wedding party in Dao. The latest film by Alain Gomis, Silver Bear winner for Félicité (2017) and a Berlinale regular, intertwines a wedding in France with a memorial ceremony in Guinea-Bissau within the same Afro-French family. At the heart of it all is a woman named Gloria, as both a mother and a daughter. More than ever, the French-Senegalese director drew from his personal experiences, before – primarily through improvisation – allowing his ensemble to explore for themselves the love and sorrow united in rituals. Gomis blends experienced actors with non-professional performers and fiction with a (‘behind the scenes’) documentary approach.

films.title: A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra
intro: A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra follows the 15-year-old titular character on a seemingly ordinary day. Until, for the first time in a long while, Jo feels a genuine connection with another person: her classmate Phaedra. Will today turn out to be different after all? If only Jo could read the life line on her palm or remember the symbols from her dream... Greek filmmaker Jacqueline Lentzou, internationally celebrated for poetic, tender cinema such as Moon, 66 Questions (FFG2021), imbues her loving teenage portrait with melancholy and mystery. Lentzou invites the viewer to join her in searching for a light that may never go out: “All we need to do is have our heart open to feel it.”
description: A film that combines the everyday and the cosmic, with humour but also roots in tragic reality.

films.title: Donn Danseur du XXe siècle (Donn Dancer of the XXth Century)
intro: At sixteen, Jorge Donn leaves Argentina for Brussels, where he becomes Maurice Béjart’s muse, lover and star dancer. Drawing on rare archival footage, Florencia Dávila and Mariano Baez bring this legendary performer vividly back to life: a body in perpetual motion, propelled by an almost inexhaustible need to dance.
description: At sixteen, Jorge Donn left Argentina for Brussels, determined to dance with Maurice Béjart's Ballet du XXe Siècle. A rejection did not deter him. Donn went on to become the company's star, finding in Béjart not only a choreographer but also a lover and artistic soulmate. With his mesmerising interpretation of Ravel's Boléro, he won over audiences worldwide. Florencia Dávila and Mariano Baez draw on an astonishing archive to bring Donn's life back into motion. His voice, gaze and body tell the story of an artist who gave male dance a new face: powerful yet vulnerable, virtuosic yet sensual. Just as Donn reaches the height of his career, AIDS begins to ravage his body. He continues to dance until the very end. Donn, danseur du XXe siècle is a compelling portrait of an exceptional artist for whom living and moving were scarcely distinguishable from one another.

films.title: Éric Rohmer, esprit d'enfance (Éric Rohmer, The spirit of childhood)
intro: Through the detailed observation of Éric Rohmer's childhood home, interwoven with film clips, rare interviews and screentests, this delicate documentary explores the particularities of the creative process of the Nouvelle Vague’s most elusive auteur. It forms both a perfect introduction to and in-depth exploration of Rohmer's enthralling cinematic universe.
description: The much-loved French filmmaker Éric Rohmer kept his private life (which he led as Maurice Schérer) strictly separate from his role as a filmmaker. In their documentary, Pascale Bouhénic and Rohmer biographer Noël Herpe do not seek to erase that separation, but rather to identify the point where the boundary becomes blurred. This leads them to Rohmer’s childhood home and the question: what can this place teach us about his cinema? We follow the patterns on the wallpaper, listen to the clinking of his collection of teapots and leaf through his diaries and school reports. Rohmer’s childhood (“esprit d’enfance”) is approached here not as a biographical fact but as an applied method that makes his films so delightfully distinctive. It is said that every collaboration with Rohmer began with a steaming cup of tea. The documentary opens with an equally warm invitation: “Come and have a cup of tea with Rohmer and step into his cinema.”

films.title: Everytime
intro: Sandra Wollner’s Everytime explores grief through an unconventional family dynamic. After a devastating incident involving 16-year-old Jessie, her mother Ella turns to Lux, the boy who spent that fatal night with Jessie. Rather than blaming him, she invites him to Tenerife with her younger daughter Melli, on a holiday that was originally planned for Jessie. The trip reveals how differently people respond to loss, guilt and the need to move on. Wollner avoids emotional manipulation, evoking a sense of unease through her restrained visual style and subtle performances. Winner of The Un Certain Regard Prize at Cannes, Everytime raises questions rather than offering comforting answers.
description: Wollner masterfully succeeds in infusing everyday events with a simmering sense of unease.

imdb.title: Everytime

films.title: Fatherland
intro: In 1949, author Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika set out to travel through Germany – their homeland, now in ruins, divided and alien to them. Will they emerge unscathed from the wreckage of history and their family? Following the equally moving, beautifully painful Ida (2013) and Cold War (crowned Best Film at FFG2018), Polish filmmaker Paweł Pawlikowski returns to Cold War Europe to devastating effect. At Cannes, it won him the Best Director award for the second time, and Sandra Hüller further solidifies her status. Freely inspired by a turbulent chapter in the life of one of the 20th century’s greatest writers, road movie Fatherland proves that emotions always find their way back home.
description: In its serene surrender, the film finds a fragile beauty and solace.

films.title: Everybody Digs Bill Evans
intro: What happens when the music suddenly stops? In 1961, jazz pianist Bill Evans loses his bassist and closest musical companion, Scott LaFaro. Evans stops playing too. Grant Gee turns that silence into the starting point for an unconventional biopic, led by a phenomenal Anders Danielsen Lie as the brilliant yet troubled pianist. Winner of the Silver Bear for Best Director.
description: New York, 1961. Bill Evans has found his musical voice – and his dream trio. During a legendary series of concerts at the Village Vanguard, Evans, drummer Paul Motian and bassist Scott LaFaro record two albums in a single day that will go down in jazz history. Ten days later, LaFaro is killed in a car accident. Paralysed by grief, Evans does not touch his piano for months. Grant Gee, known for music documentaries such as Joy Division, makes that abrupt silence the beating heart of an unconventional biopic. Based on Owen Martell’s novel Intermission and carried by a phenomenal Anders Danielsen Lie, the film moves associatively through Evans’ life. Bathed in high-contrast black and white, it shifts between intoxication and clarity, family and music, self-destruction and the urge to create. Gee, awarded the Silver Bear for Best Director, looks beyond the familiar image of the tortured genius to the human being behind the piano.

imdb.title: Everybody Digs Bill Evans

films.title: La femme de l’aviateur (The Aviator's Wife)
intro: With The Aviator's Wife, Rohmer embarks on a new cycle: Comedies and Proverbs. This series is less cerebral than Rohmer's Moral Tales, as this film immediately demonstrates. A light-hearted and subtle comedy about jealousy, misunderstandings and falling in love, in which an everyday quest develops into a thrilling game of interpretation and chance.
description: With The Aviator's Wife, Rohmer launches the Comédies et proverbes (Comedy and Proverbs) cycle, shifting the focus from philosophical reflections to the observation of behaviour, chance and misunderstandings. François, a postman, suspects that his girlfriend Anne is back together with her ex, a pilot (Mathieu Carrière), and begins to shadow him. Together with the curious teenager Lucie, he weaves a playful detective fantasy that primarily lays bare their own imaginations. Rohmer thus creates a subtle suspense film without a crime, in which misinterpretation takes centre stage. The Parc des Buttes-Chaumont becomes the setting for an everyday poetry in which a budding relationship develops almost imperceptibly. As is often the case with Rohmer, La femme de l’aviateur is at once light as a feather and profoundly serious. Shot on location on grainy 16 mm film, the film marks Rohmer’s return to the austere style of the Nouvelle Vague.

films.title: Le genou de Claire (Claire's Knee)
intro: This film, which is both sensual and philosophical, explores morality, desire and a sensual obsession; it is the fifth in the cycle Six Contes moraux. Once again, the protagonist is plagued by an all-consuming fixation: he is determined to touch the knee of a teenage girl. The obsession develops into a delicate exploration of the boundaries of seduction and self-delusion.
description: The fifth instalment of the Six contes moraux revolves around a seemingly trivial, compulsive desire: the diplomat Jérôme (Jean-Claude Brialy) is determined, at any cost, to touch the young Claire’s knee. Whilst his fiancée is away, he flirts with various women during a summer spent at Lake Annecy. His fascination with Claire’s knee develops into a moral and emotional dilemma. Rohmer transforms this seemingly trivial premise into a subtle study of seduction, sensual obsession and self-deception, wrapped in a delightful ethical suspense. The writer Aurora acts as a sounding board for Jérôme’s endless self-analysis, whilst Nestor Almendros’s transparent colour photography brings the languid summer atmosphere to life. The result is one of Rohmer’s most sensual and crystal-clear films, in which he also brilliantly brings together people and landscape.

films.title: La Gradiva
intro: Cinematographer Marine Atlan makes a spellbinding feature debut with La Gradiva, following a group of French final-year students on a school trip to Naples and Pompeii. As their teacher Mercier, superbly played by Antonia Buresi, tries to inspire them with frescoes and volcanoes, the young cast of mostly newcomers are far more absorbed in one another. Friendships, desire and sexuality shift and collide as Atlan captures the intensity, vulnerability and occasional cruelty of life on the cusp of adulthood. Under the Italian sun, insecurities and frustrations simmer against the timeless backdrop of a city once buried beneath ash.
description: A sensual coming-of-age that takes the intense emotions of adolescence deadly seriously, set against the intoxicating backdrop of Pompeii.

films.title: Gugu's world (9+) (Feito Pipa)
intro: Colourful twelve-year-old Gugu loves football … and his caring but increasingly frail grandmother Dilma with whom he shares a house. But when Dilma’s age catches up, Gugu is determined to keep their world intact. A radiant queer coming-of-ager from Brazil, Gugu’s World proves that – time after time – love and understanding conquer all.
description: If it were up to Gugu, he’d save the world single-handedly. The nearly twelve-year-old lad has loads of self-confidence, stands up for himself and is just comfortably himself. Like any Brazilian child, Gugu wants to become a footballer. Although that’s not exactly a given for someone from a small, rural community near a fictional reserve that’s drying up, gradually revealing a sunken city. Even more than football, Gugu loves his grandmother Dilma, with whom he lives. Their tender bond shields him from his father’s disapproval and from bullies. Together in their cosy home, the two seem invincible. But as Dilma, who is suffering from dementia, becomes more vulnerable, Gugu faces the prospect of having to leave the only place where he is understood. With imagery as colourful as its main character, Gugu’s World blossoms into an authentic coming-of-age film.

Heaven Will Wait is a hybrid documentary about the tension between sexual autonomy and objectification: the women are aware of the gaze that sexualizes them, yet still long for the validation it offers.

films.title: Un Jeune Homme de Bonne Famille (A Very Good Boy)
intro: French director Sébastien Lifshitz returns to Film Fest Gent with a portrait of 82-year-old Claude Loir, a former porn actor and early figure in the gay liberation movement. Drawing on Loir’s autobiography, the documentary traces a life shaped by his determination to embrace pleasure and freedom in France of the late 1960s and early 1970s.
description: French director Sébastien Lifshitz is a regular guest at Film Fest Gent. Six years after winning the Grand Prix for Best Film for Petite fille, he presents a new documentary this year, Un jeune homme de bonne famille. In it, he portrays 82-year-old Claude Loir, a former porn actor and, more than half a century ago, a figurehead of gay liberation. Lifshitz got to know Loir three years ago when he published his autobiography Confessions païennes (Pagan Confessions). In Un jeune homme de bonne famille, Lifshitz offers a faithful account of the man's life. Loir's drive to embrace life to the fullest has always shaped his choices and forms the thread running through his existence – however difficult that was in the late '60s and early '70s, in a France torn between extreme conservatism (the shadow of Charles de Gaulle) and the sexual liberation of May '68.

films.title: A. Rimbaud
intro: Patrick Wang throws all cinematic conventions out the window, rekindling the fire of Arthur Rimbaud’s imagination with the barest of means. A black box becomes a bar, a street, a hell - and music gives voice to the people who surround Rimbaud. Without a doubt one of the most radical and singular films of this festival edition.
description: Arthur Rimbaud was the rock star of French poetry: a brilliant bad boy who shook literature to its foundations as a teenager, only to turn his back on it completely at the age of twenty. In A. Rimbaud, Patrick Wang captures that restless spirit in a bold, almost three-hour cinematic trip. The film takes place almost entirely within a stark black box, where a single actor embodies Rimbaud and all the other characters are brought to life through musical instruments. The result is as theatrical as it is cinematic, as playful as it is austere. Wang, known for his grand two-part epic A Bread Factory (2018), about the resilience of art and community, once again embraces a form that defies convention. From the nights in Paris and Rimbaud’s tempestuous relationship with Paul Verlaine to his later life as a trader in Africa, A. Rimbaud is no conventional biopic, but an uncompromising attempt to make palpable the spirit of an elusive poet.

films.title: Iron Boy (7+) (Le Corset)
intro: When 11-year-old Christophe is forced to wear an iron corset, he discovers an unexpected refuge in music. Inspired by animator and Pixar veteran Louis Clichy's own childhood in the French countryside, Iron Boy is a tender, hand-drawn coming-of-age tale about the longing to break free. A watercolour painting that contrasts the economic realities of farm life with the boundless hopes of a young boy.
description: Eleven-year-old Christophe is bored stiff on his strict father’s farm. Suddenly, he starts falling over for no apparent reason, everywhere and all the time. The solution? An orthopaedic corset. Whilst his older brother works himself to the bone on the farm, Christophe discovers a new passion: the church organ. The solo debut of animator and Pixar veteran Louis Clichy, who still wears a corset to this day, is an expressive and personal work of art. Watercolour, Chinese ink, spontaneous sketches and a dash of classical music bring the French countryside of the 1980s to life, where the harsh economic reality of farm life clashes with Christophe’s imagination and thirst for freedom. The heart-warming Iron Boy hovers somewhere between nostalgia, memory and imagination, and shows that turning the world upside down isn’t such a crazy idea after all. A captivating watercolour film that won a jury prize at the Cannes Film Festival. At the recent international animation film festival in Annecy, Iron Boy furthermore received both the jury prize and the audience award.

intro: When the little hippo Mumbo grows to giant size, he has to go on a dangerous journey with his three friends to find the witch Baba Yaga so she can turn him small again. Based on Jakob Martin Strid’s children’s book, this adventure might make Mumbo small again, but a whole lot bigger on the inside.
description: The young hippopotamus Mumbo is too small to help with the preparations for the village festival. If only he were a bit bigger, he’d feel so much more useful! But when Mumbo picks and eats a magic mushroom, he becomes so enormous that he can’t even sleep in his mum’s bed anymore. Suddenly, he realises that being big isn’t so easy after all. The only one who can make him small again? The witch Baba Yaga, who lives miles away, in a little house on stilts in a dark forest. And so Mumbo has no choice but to set off in search of Baba Yaga, travelling along busy motorways, across deep waters and through dangerous forests. Fortunately, he can count on his brave friends Cheetah, Tapir and the little blue elephant Mimbo. This charming animated film is based on the much-loved children’s book by the Danish children’s author Jakob Martin Strid and is perfect for anyone who wants to learn that just being yourself is grand enough.

She wanted to show the diversity in a women's audience, the sophistication, the thoughtfulness, the fun-loving spirit, the flirtations, the detailed, the subtle. She wanted her audience to make their own film.In a time of national borders and increasing geographic chauvinism, she found images of women transcending boundaries and cultures and at the same time acting as spokespeople for cultural difference.

films.title: Snow Job: The Media Hysteria of AIDS
description: Barbara Hammer first heard of AIDS in 1985 while she was teaching at Columbia College in Chicago. She noticed the strange and inflammatory articles appearing in newspapers and asked her students to collect hysterical headlines for her. This marked the beginning of her work on Snow Job: The Media Hysteria of AIDS. In this project, she examined the public ignorance, stigmatization, and fundamentally misguided attitudes surrounding the new illness. By creating a snowstorm of newspaper clippings, she aimed to reveal the extent to which the media was producing a “snow job”.

films.title: L'ami de mon amie (Boyfriends and Girlfriends)
intro: The sixth and final film in the Comédies et proverbes series is a charming comedy about love, self-deception and unfulfilled desires, in which Rohmer observes human relationships and chance encounters through delightful dialogue and refined visual language.
description: The final instalment of Comédies et proverbes is a subtle comedy about love, chance and self-deception. The introverted Blanche (Emmanuelle Chaulet) befriends the spontaneous Léa and becomes entangled in a subtle love quadrangle with Alexandre and Fabien. As is often the case with Rohmer, the tension lies not in the plot, but in the dialogue, glances and subtle shifts in the relationships between the young lovers. Particularly striking is the role played by Cergy-Pontoise, the modernist and somewhat sterile satellite town whose clean postmodern architecture contrasts with the characters’ emotional uncertainty and the vagaries of the heart. Once again, Rohmer allows emotion and logic to clash cheerfully and weaves setting and psychology into a refined whole. Colour, composition and natural performances lend this seemingly simple film a great visual elegance. Thus, the director concludes his second cycle with one of his most harmonious and refreshing films.

films.title: 9 Temples to Heaven
intro: In Thailand, some Buddhists believe that visiting nine temples can increase karma. When businessman Sakol learns his mother may soon die, he takes his family on a pilgrimage. What starts as a search for protection becomes a subtle exploration of faith, family and meaning in a changing society. A contemplative road movie about belief and human connection.
description: In Thailand, some Buddhists believe that you can improve your karma by visiting nine temples in a single day. When the businessman Sakol hears from a clairvoyant that his mother is about to die, he doesn’t hesitate for a second. He piles into a minibus with three generations of his family. It soon becomes clear that his mother is the least enthusiastic about this pilgrimage. What begins as an attempt to secure prosperity and protection develops into a subtle exploration of family ties and the search for meaning in a changing society. 9 Temples to Heaven is the feature film debut of Sompot Chidgasornpongse, the former assistant to Palme d’Or winner Apichatpong Weerasethakul. Although more down-to-earth than Weerasethakul’s work, 9 Temples to Heaven does contain some echoes of his style. Nevertheless, this contemplative road movie, which playfully asks what faith still means today, is much more than a mere imitation of the master.

films.title: L'âge d'or (The Golden Age)
intro: An ambitious butcher’s daughter works her way up in society during the twentieth century, all the while confronted with the great upheavals of that time, in Bérenger Thouin’s L’Âge d’or. Using both fictional and archival material, this instant Classic at Cannes challenges our ideas of wealth, success and happiness, while providing an existential trip through time.
description: A young woman born into humble circumstances dreams of a better life, but is confronted with the sacrifices involved in achieving that ambition. The premise of L’Âge d'or appears deceptively conventional, but make no mistake: in his feature debut, Bérenger Thouin effortlessly turns the typical ‘zero to hero’ narrative on its head. The Franco-Italian director spent over ten years working on this remarkable fictional epic, which chronicles the aspirations of Jeanne Lavaur, the daughter of a butcher. She guides us through the great social upheavals of the twentieth century, driven by an insatiable hunger for power and a dubious moral compass. Thouin presents Jeanne’s life story in beautiful vignettes, composed of a mix of archive footage and new material. The result is a complex portrait, worthy of a premiere in the Classics section at Cannes.

films.title: Aro berria
intro: What if the revolution begins not on the factory floor, but in your own body? In the Basque Country of 1978, a group of workers trade political struggle for a radical experiment that extends the revolution into their relationships, desires and bodies. Irati Gorostidi makes a provocative debut about idealism and the old patterns that prove so difficult to shake off.
description: In 1978, workers at a factory in Donostia, in the Spanish Basque Country, are debating a strike that ultimately never happens. For the most radical among them, fighting for better working conditions is no longer enough. As the revolution stalls on the factory floor, they seek it elsewhere: in a community in the mountains, where young people experiment with communal living, spirituality and sexual liberation. Love, possession and the limits of the body become a grey area.

For her feature debut, Irati Gorostidi draws on almost ten years of research into Basque counterculture, to which she also has a personal connection: her own parents lived in such a community. Aro berria moves from the greyness of the factory to the green of the countryside, without turning that new freedom into an idyll. Political conviction clashes with desire, the collective with the individual. Old power structures do not simply get left behind.

imdb.title: Aro berria
imdb.plot: Water meter factory workers hold an assembly about a strike, which fails. Disappointed, the non-conformist workers turn to more personal realms. Some leave to join a mountain community, where young people share cathartic experiences.

films.title: La bola negra (The Black Ball)
intro: Queer epic La bola negra breathes new life into unfinished work by Federico García Lorca. Filmmakers Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, awarded Best Director at Cannes, explore and celebrate the interconnected stories of three gay men across different eras in Spain. A moving and magnificent account of their sexual identity, their desires, their pain, and their legacy.
description: Before he was murdered at the start of the Spanish Civil War, the openly gay writer Federico García Lorca penned the first four pages of the novel La bola negra. The title refers to the social exclusion of a gay character. Ninety years later, filmmakers Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi are reclaiming the queer history of their homeland. For some time now, the duo have been actively contributing to greater representation of the LGBTQIA+ community in Spanish art, culture and media. Inspired by García Lorca’s unfinished work and a play by co-screenwriter Alberto Conejero, they explore, connect and celebrate the lives of three gay men in 1932, 1937 and 2017. Their ambitious and compelling epic, shot on 35mm film, proudly pays homage to classic melodrama with a contemporary flair. This earned them the Best Director Award at Cannes, shared with Paweł Pawlikowski for Fatherland (also screening at this edition of the FFG).

imdb.title: La bola negra
imdb.plot: Explores what it means to be gay throughout different eras, focusing on "three existences" that are connected through themes of sexuality, desire, pain, and inheritance.

films.title: Breendonk - Episode 1
intro: Belgium under Nazi occupation, 1942. Resistance fighter Rik and his father Leon are imprisoned in the brutal Breendonk camp, where survival comes at a devastating price. Forced into a dangerous alliance with a Flemish SS guard, they face impossible choices between loyalty, betrayal and survival. A powerful drama inspired by true events.
description: Love, betrayal and survival collide head-on in Breendonk, a gripping series set in occupied Belgium in 1942. When resistance fighters Rik and Elisabeth are torn apart by the war, Rik ends up, along with his father Leon, in the notorious 'Auffanglager Breendonk' camp, where the SS attempt to break prisoners through forced labour, humiliation and arbitrary violence. To survive, Rik and Leon strike a devilish pact with a Flemish SS guard who is playing a double game. Whilst the war rages outside the camp walls, every choice within the camp – to remain silent, to help, to betray or to obey – becomes a matter of life or death. Breendonk is an ambitious series, inspired by true events and filmed on location. It stars a remarkable duo: Koen and Jolan De Bouw, father and son, both in the series and in real life. Film Fest Gent is screening the first two episodes in premiere.

intro: Twin sisters Jean and Joan (Kate and Rooney Mara) speak in unison, dream the same dreams and love the same man… who is taking them to court. A strange but - mostly - true story, that’s tailor-made for Werner Herzog. Bucking Fastard premiered at the Venice Film Festival, where in 2025 the iconic German director was awarded the Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement.

films.title: Burgundy
intro: In Burgundy, acclaimed documentarians Michael Dweck and Gregory Kershaw (The Truffle Hunters, Gaucho Gaucho) follow different generations of French winegrowers, sommeliers and waiters in the renowned wine region as they struggle to find their own place in an ever-changing world. Make no mistake: this seemingly light wine has a surprisingly full-bodied flavour. Santé!
description: Set in the world-famous wine region of Burgundy, Burgundy takes a look at the often eccentric figures involved in the centuries-old process of producing the very best wines. It explores both the day-to-day struggles of the veterans and the grand dreams of the novices learning the trade from them. It’s not all sunshine and roses; sometimes you taste cork, too. The poetic documentary style of the American duo Michael Dweck and Gregory Kershaw has come to fruition in recent years in The Truffle Hunters (2020) and Gaucho Gaucho (2024). With their discerning eye (Dweck is an acclaimed photographer), a subtle touch of retro and self-deprecating humour, they cheerfully observe the tension between tradition and innovation. In the words of wine merchant Bertrand: "Great wine is the sum of details, each of which has little meaning, but when combined, everything changes." Burgundy raises a glass to love and passion with a bittersweet aftertaste.

films.title: Club Kid
intro: A crowd-pleasing dramedy that is both cheeky and genuinely endearing? Club Kid is a treat for those who like being charmed yet still want something different. Queer comedian and screenwriter Jordan Firstman directs himself as an aging New York party animal who discovers he’s a father. At Cannes, the film grabbed attention as a gay take on Adam Sandler's Big Daddy.
description: Party animal Peter grew up in New York’s hedonistic nightlife, but his best years are behind him. The party seems to be well and truly over when the single thirty-something suddenly receives a visit from ten-year-old Arlo, a son he didn’t even know existed. Or is this actually a chance to finally grow up? Club Kid openly flirts with the familiar formula of American comedy-dramas, only to cleverly surprise the viewer in the end. That is the charm and talent of Jordan Firstman, who wrote the screenplay, takes on the lead role and delivers his first feature film as director. The versatile comedian made a name for himself with sitcoms, web series and even Instagram sketches during lockdown, often inspired by his experiences as a gay man and peppered with cheeky humour. No wonder that, following the premiere in Cannes, film distributors were fighting amongst themselves for this authentic-feeling queer comedy with a big heart.

films.title: Bunker
intro: When architect Miguel is commissioned to build a luxurious bunker for a select group of the super-rich, he faces an uncomfortable choice: does he help build a shelter for the privileged few, or walk away? Florian Zeller turns this moral dilemma into a paranoid psychological thriller about power, fear and mistrust.
description: A tech billionaire has a bunker built to survive the impending end of the world: does he know something we don’t? Florian Zeller (The Son, FFG2022) takes this unsettling question as the starting point for a paranoid thriller about mistrust, inequality and fear of the future. Architect Miguel (Javier Bardem) is commissioned to design a luxurious shelter for a select group of the ultra-rich, a modern pyramid for a new pharaoh. Paul Dano is fantastic as the terrifying billionaire, a paranoid, out-of-touch creep clearly modelled on tech moguls like Zuckerberg and Musk. But that paranoia also seeps into Miguel and Sofia’s (Penélope Cruz) marriage. After seventeen years together, their relationship becomes a mirror of the world they live in: a world in which we increasingly trust no one.

films.title: Dua
intro: Set in late-1990s Kosovo, Blerta Basholli's personal coming-of-age drama follows a 13-year-old girl whose search for independence unfolds as her country edges towards war. Led by impressive newcomer Pinea Matoshi and selected as Kosovo's official Oscar submission, is a poignant, tense portrait of childhood, family, friendship and identity caught in the tide of socio-political upheaval.
description: Being a teenager is chaos. Let alone having to spend that time in a conflict zone. Thirteen-year-old Dua lives with her family in Pristina, the capital of Kosovo, in the late 1990s, when Serbian troops were brutally persecuting the Albanian majority. Through her eyes, we see how parties and school life become impossible as danger creeps ever deeper into her life. Inspired by director Blerta Basholli’s own memories, her second feature film poignantly captures the clash between a carefree childhood and a country on the brink of collapse. Through long takes and fluid camera movements, we observe alongside Dua as ethnic tensions cause judo halls to empty and leave entire households in fear. Following her acclaimed debut Hive (2021), about the aftermath of the Kosovo War, Basholli puts Kosovar cinema back on the map with this coming-of-age portrait, which she says was influenced by the Dardenne brothers.

films.title: Donkey Princess (Princesa Burro)
intro: After the death of her mother, Diana’s father bans love throughout the kingdom. Ignoring his decree, she sets off in search of Lalo, the man she longs for, travelling through parallel worlds along the way. What starts as a fairy-tale romance unfolds into a wildly imaginative journey where reality, fantasy and the unexpected constantly collide.
description: The title already gives it away: Donkey Princess is a fairy tale. But a fairy tale of a kind you rarely get to see. The Chilean directing duo Cristóbal León and Joaquín Cociña, with a background in stop-motion animation, take Charles Perrault's Peau d'Âne (Donkeyskin) as their starting point but turn it inside out. The donkey princess' name is Diana (no, she has nothing to do with Lady Di), who is at loggerheads with her father over the man she has her eye on, Lalo. Following the death of his wife, the king has, in fact, imposed a ban on love. Diana cheerfully ignores this and journeys through parallel worlds in search of Lalo. Donkey Princess begins as a forbidden romance, but soon transforms into an extremely imaginative quest through time and space, in which live action, stop-motion animation and surreal imagery blend seamlessly into one another. A wild, cinematic trip from an exceptionally talented directing duo.

imdb.title: Donkey Princess
imdb.plot: Follows Princess Diana in a kingdom where her father outlawed love. At 15, she falls for Lalo, who is banished. Diana uses a magical bracelet to travel across worlds searching for her lost love.

films.title: The Education of Jane Cumming
intro: Edinburgh, 1810. A scandal breaks out in a boardingschool for girls when two female teachers are accused of having a love affaire. Based on a true story, this elegant queer costume drama thrives on the simmering tensions between its characters and depicts both the struggle to love unconditionally, free from societal constraints, as the scars that result from it.
description: A dream comes true for Jane Pirie (Flora Nicholson) and Marianne Woods (Clare Dunne) when they open their girls’ boarding school. The school gets off to a modest start but gains prestige when Lady Cumming Gordon (Fiona Shaw) enrols her granddaughters there, including Jane Cumming (Mia Tharia). The fifteen-year-old pupil is half-Indian and was born out of wedlock, which prompts her peers to bully her. With her teachers, Jane finds the understanding and sense of home she has been missing since the early death of her parents. Their bond grows stronger during a summer spent together, but soon begins to fray when boundaries are set. The true story of Pirie and Woods has already been adapted several times, but German filmmaker Sophie Heldman sheds new light on it by focusing on the love between Pirie and Woods and their struggle to lead a free and independent life.

films.title: Everybody to Kenmure Street
intro: On a quiet street in Glasgow, an ordinary morning turns into an extraordinary act of resistance. In Everybody to Kenmure Street, Felipe Bustos Sierra reconstructs how a diverse community comes together to prevent the deportation of two neighbours. A compelling portrait of solidarity, civil courage and the power of collective action.
description: In May 2021, a quiet morning on Kenmure Street, Glasgow, is abruptly disrupted when the UK Home Office attempts to arrest and deport two residents. The news spreads rapidly via messages and social media: neighbours leave their homes, work and daily routines to gather around the police van. What begins as a spontaneous reaction grows into a massive, peaceful blockade. Using smartphone footage from those present, archive material and testimonies – including a remarkable narration by Emma Thompson – Felipe Bustos Sierra reconstructs this extraordinary day. He situates the event within the long history of resistance and solidarity in Glasgow, from labour movements to contemporary activism. Everybody to Kenmure Street is not only a compelling account of civil disobedience, but also a hopeful portrait of a community that demonstrates the power of collective action.

imdb.title: Everybody to Kenmure Street
imdb.plot: Glasgow residents abandon their daily routines to gather on Kenmure Street after learning authorities plan to deport their neighbors, sparking an impromptu grassroots movement.

films.title: L'estranea (The Spiral)
intro: During a stormy night in Rome, Anna confesses to her daughter Alice that she made a pact with a stranger twenty years ago. Ever since, a curse has hung over the family. She begs Alice for help... For the promising Italian director Paolo Strippoli, this dramatic horror story marks an international breakthrough. Sought after by Venice, Toronto and... Ghent.
description: Anna and her family have found themselves caught in a downward spiral. To break free from it, she confesses to her daughter Alice that she once struck a deal with a stranger, which now hangs over the family like a curse. Only Alice can provide a way out. But is she willing to do so? And at what cost? For 33-year-old Italian Paolo Strippoli, a mother-daughter relationship is a compelling starting point for sketching out a powerfully dramatic family saga. For Strippoli, horror is not merely horror. He uses it to lay bare wounds, to question family values, and to reflect on power and powerlessness in life. It’s perfectly fine to be spooked, and in that respect you get more than your money’s worth cinematically. No wonder, then, that L’Estranea secured a place in the Venice Film Festival competition. Those seeking added value in all this need only imagine Thomas Mann’s the Buddenbrooks meets Dr Faustus. This time set in Bari and Rome.

imdb.title: The Spiral
