films.title: Everything Else Is Noise (Lo demás es ruido)
intro: Everything Else Is Noise by Mexican filmmaker Nicolás Pereda is a minimalist film set mainly in one apartment, which uses an interview setting to ironically dissect themes as artistic pretension, sexism and patriarchy. Thanks to a brilliant mix of (cello) music, traffic, barking dogs and everyday noise, the sound design is the true protagonist of this tragicomedy.
description: A static shot lasting more than four minutes of traffic chaos at a busy junction, whilst the honking of vehicles and the sounds of a melancholic cello blend into a sorrowful sonata: that is all Mexican director Nicolás Pereda needs to draw you into Everything Else Is Noise (Lo demás es ruido). Tere, a sharp-witted cellist who is having trouble with her neighbours, welcomes a friend into her flat who gets interviewed by two journalists. Tere and her daughter Luisa are more than mere spectators. With wry, cutting commentary, they mock art snobs, expose sexism and denounce the patriarchy. But the real starring role is reserved for sound. Music, silence, traffic noise, dogs and distracting ambient sounds do not merely form the backdrop, but dictate the film’s rhythm. Everyday sounds take on an almost musical quality. Listening is just as important as watching.

imdb.title: Everything Else Is Noise
imdb.plot: In Mexico, musician Tere hosts fellow composer Rosa for a TV interview. Their conversation wanders as unexpected guests arrive. A witty, absurdist comedy that lampoons art-world phoniness and pretension while honoring female friendship.

films.title: Filipiñana
intro: A scorching slow-burn on the golf course. In Filipiñana, a teenager working at a prestigious golf club learns the unspoken rules of their exclusive little world. Secrets buried deep beneath the perfectly maintained green. With this treacherously leisurely feature debut, Filipino director Rafael Manuel reworks his award-winning 2020 short film of the same name.
description: Under the blazing sun, inexperienced 17-year-old Isabel works at a golf course. She finds herself inexplicably drawn to Dr Palanca, the chairman of the exclusive golf club, yet senses something sinister lurking behind the immaculate façade. Filipiñana was originally the graduation project of Filipino director Rafael Manuel, with which he won the jury prize for best short film in Berlin in 2020. Six years later, Manuel returned to the Berlinale with this feature-length debut of the same name, built around the same story. The longer running time allows him to test the elasticity of the deceptive calm associated with the luxury sport, set to the unhurried pace of hitting a ball. Underpinned by the exceptionally controlled cinematography, the calm of this microcosm conceals class divides in the Philippines, an uneasy tension, and traces of their colonial history. So subtle that it deliberately remains almost invisible.

imdb.title: Filipiñana
imdb.plot: Teen Isabel's attraction to Dr. Palanca at her country club job turns dark as she uncovers violence beneath the club's facade and discovers their disturbing connection from the past.

films.title: Fjord
intro: Inspired by true events, the moral drama Fjord pits the parenting values ​​of two conservative parents (Renate Reinsve and Sebastian Stan) against the so-called open-mindedness of their Norwegian fellow villagers. Romanian filmmaker Cristian Mungiu (4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days) masters treading on glacial ice and warmed up the jury at Cannes for a second Golden Palm.
description: Fjord reunites the versatile actors Renate Reinsve (The Worst Person in the World, FFG2021) and Sebastian Stan (The Apprentice, FFG2024), who previously starred together in A Different Man (FFG2024). The pair play a conservative couple who move with their children from Romania to the woman’s remote, progressive hometown in Norway. Instead of a warm welcome, their relationship with the villagers soon plummets below freezing. Director Cristian Mungiu is regarded as one of the leading figures of the Romanian New Wave and is a regular at Film Fest Gent, having previously screened films such as Bacalaureat (FFG2016). Fjord, inspired by a true-life drama, earned him his second Palme d’Or following 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days (2007), alongside no fewer than four other awards at Cannes. Mungiu once again delivers morally complex cinema exploring conflicting values that gives pause for thought. Chilling and powerfully executed.

imdb.title: Fjord
imdb.plot: An immigrant Romanian family living in Norway is subject to an investigation and faces the scrutiny of the local judicial system.

films.title: The Friend's House Is Here
intro: In Tehran's underground art scene, Pari and Hanna carve out a space for creativity, friendship and resistance. But freedom can never be taken for granted. Shot clandestinely in Iran, Maryam Ataei and Hossein Keshavarz's The Friend's House Is Here is a warm, urgent portrait of two women determined to hold on to their creativity – and to each other.
description: Pari runs an independent theatre company in Tehran; her best friend Hanna is a dancer who dreams of leaving Iran. Together they move through a colourful underground arts scene, where rehearsals, parties and encounters create space for freedom. When their artistic circle comes under pressure, their friendship and their futures are put to the test. Maryam Ataei and Hossein Keshavarz shot The Friend's House Is Here clandestinely in Tehran, with a cast and crew who took great risks to tell their story. Yet the film opts not for gloom, but for the zest for life of a generation that refuses to be told how to live or create. Mahshad Bahram and Hana Mana carry the film with a magnetic presence; together with the rest of the cast, they were honoured at Sundance with a Special Jury Award. A warm tribute to artistic freedom, solidarity and the power of friendship.

imdb.title: The Friend's House Is Here
imdb.plot: Two women in Tehran's underground art scene create a haven of freedom and sisterhood until their circle is discovered, forcing them to struggle for each other's survival.

films.title: Gabin
intro: In this wonderfully charming coming-of-age film, French director Maxence Voiseux paints an intimate portrait of Gabin growing up on a farm. We follow him from age 8 to adulthood, finding his way caught between his parents. His father wants him to become a butcher, but he would rather work with livestock and finds an ally in his mother. The beautiful Gabin was one of the discoveries of Cannes.
description: As we follow Gabin from the age of 8 to 18, this feature-film-style documentary is often compared to Richard Linklater’s Boyhood. Among other things, little Gabin dreams of breeding a cow to show off at livestock shows. His father would rather see him slaughter that cow, as he wants his son to take over the butcher’s trade on the farm. Otherwise, he’ll set the place on fire. Gabin must navigate his way to adulthood whilst dealing with his parents. A journey that involves saying goodbye. Subtlety is the hallmark of director Maxence Voiseux. Small touches in the costumes and the setting ensure that we see Gabin grow up almost imperceptibly in the delightful-looking north of France. There’s even an abbey involved. One of the lovely surprises in this sometimes moving chronicle of its time.

imdb.title: Gabin
imdb.plot: Torn between family loyalty and his desire for freedom, Gabin observes over ten years a boy fighting to emancipate himself from his working-class background in the rural North of France.

films.title: Forêt Ivre (Forest High)
intro: Three women each choose solitude in their own way by retreating to the same mountain. Although they never meet, they sense each other’s presence as their different lives enter into a whispered dialogue. Belgium-based director Manon Coubia beautifully invigorates the current film landscape with this sublime debut fiction film in which one will want to dwell endlessly.
description: Anne, Hélène and Suzanne are staying on a mountain as "gardiennes de refuge", where they are responsible for maintaining a mountain hut and welcoming the walkers who stay there overnight. The women’s experiences are separated in time, but linked by the place and the small actions they carry out there. Every presence lingers in the thin air; every step taken is imprinted on the wooden floorboards. Shrouded in the silence of the night, the place speaks of the present and the past. Forêt Ivre is steeped in a love of analogue film and stories rooted in specific places that impose their own pace and customs. The work of seasoned short-film director Manon Coubia has been featured in our short-film competition right from the very beginning (2016, 2019, 2023). With her feature-length fiction debut, Coubia demonstrates that, even in this format, she promises to be one of the most remarkable names on the Belgian film scene.

screenings.guests: Anne Coesens (Cast), Manon Coubia (Director, Screenplay), Salomé Richard (Cast), Alba Rincon Coubia (Cast), Yoann Zimmer (Cast), Aline Huber (Sound Designer), Arthur Marbaix (Cast), Robin Fresson (Camera (DOP)), Theophile Gay-Mazas (Editor), Vincent Nouaille (Sound Designer), Tom Durand-Bonnard (Producer)

imdb.title: Forest High
imdb.plot: Three women rotate caring for an Alpine hut. As hikers pass through the seasons, tales emerge and dissolve, leaving them to contemplate their solitary lives amid nature's poetry.

films.title: The History of Concrete
intro: With The History of Concrete, American director John Wilson leaves his handprint in the cement of creative documentaries. Embarrassed to know so little about the building material, he embarks on a surprising quest that is anything but grey in his distinctive narrative style. Disarmingly contemplative, unpredictable and witty, Wilson crafts a gift of a film.
description: Anyone expecting The History of Concrete to be a ponderous documentary clearly hasn’t encountered American director John Wilson. Just as in his idiosyncratic HBO series How To with John Wilson, his curious mind is always prone to wandering off on unexpected tangents. In order to get a project about the history of concrete off the ground, he turns to the cheesy TV movies of the Hallmark Channel. The result is a series of wonderfully bizarre detours (3D-printed Starbucks, gum removers, Christmas music by gangsta rapper DMX, Tibetan sand mandalas), as well as disarming insights into the literal and figurative cracks in a concrete world.With Wilson narrating in the second person, the film offers a human perspective on America from the inside, with tonnes of humour holding it all together. Surprisingly reminiscent in style of the documentaries of Agnès Varda. From the most unexpected of places comes a feel-good film for anyone who feels stuck. But nothing is set in stone – or cast in concrete.

imdb.title: The History of Concrete
imdb.plot: A filmmaker applies lessons from a Hallmark movie writing workshop to pitch a documentary about concrete.

films.title: Das geträumte Abenteuer (The Dreamed Adventure)
intro: Small-town crime has never felt more palpable than in Valeska Grisebach’s Western follow-up Das Geträumte Abenteuer (The Dreamed Adventure). The rickety yet charming Bulgarian city Svilengrad serves as the perfect backdrop for a naturalistic slow-burn thriller that dissects morality, gender dynamics and authenticity in the face of hardship.
description: In Svilengrad, crime is a constant and palpable presence. The Bulgarian town begins where the law ends, or so the local mantra goes. Its inhabitants do what they can to survive, cautiously manoeuvring between the shadowy activities of local kingpins and occasionally confessing their sins in trusted company, in the dark and accompanied by copious amounts of alcohol. Veska, an archaeologist with roots in the region, manages to hold her own with a gentle smile in the lawless border town, until a former associate disappears in disturbing circumstances. Suddenly, the sharp-witted archaeologist finds herself forced to uncover not only her archaeological site, but also a complex criminal network. In anyone else’s hands, this premise might herald a blockbuster gangster film, but German filmmaker Valeska Grisebach opts for a radically different approach. As in her previous film Western, Grisebach infuses this naturalistic neo-noir with political commentary. Under her direction, Das Geträumte Abenteuer becomes a slow-burning, sensual thriller filled with charged conversations and simmering tension.

imdb.title: The Dreamed Adventure
imdb.plot: A woman who agrees to a deal to help an old acquaintance. She follows the hero on his adventure and enters dangerous territory where she is then confronted with her own desire.

films.title: How to Divorce During the War
intro: As if a divorce isn’t destabilising enough, Lithuanian couple Marija and Vytas find themselves grappling with the unraveling of their marriage during political turmoil in this loaded, subdued satire. Set in Vilnius right after Russia invades Ukraine, How to Divorce During the War provides insight into the parallels between marital and geopolitical discord.
description: Vilnius, 2022. Whilst their daughter Dovile unsuspectingly plays the violin, her parents Marija and Vytas are ending their marriage. There is no time to come to terms with this personal drama; barely 24 hours later, Russia invades Ukraine. Suddenly, the couple are confronted with tensions and conflicts on both a small and a large scale. Award-winning director Andrius Blaževičius’s How to Divorce During the War is a pitch-black dramedy that reveals the petty sides of people in crisis. For instance, a few weeks after her triumphant resignation, Marija returns, tail between her legs, to her employer, a social media company with Russian connections. Vytas, too, is forced to swallow his pride when he has no choice but to move in with his pro-Russian parents. Blaževičius portrays the Lithuanian duo in all their clumsiness. This makes How to Divorce During the War a sharp, humorous and empathetic analysis of people on a knife's edge.

imdb.title: How to Divorce During the War
imdb.plot: Set in Vilnius in 2022, high-flying executive Marija chooses the worst moment to discuss divorce with husband Vytas - one day before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The couple navigates separation amid a refugee crisis.

films.title: If I Go Will They Miss Me
intro: After serving time in prison, Big Ant returns home to Watts, Los Angeles, where his relationship with his twelve-year-old son remains fragile. Lil Ant seeks affection, while his father pushes him to be tougher. Inspired by Greek mythology, the boy escapes into vivid fantasies, giving this father-son story a distinctive touch of gentle surrealism.
description: "He's home again from the Trojan War, like Odysseus." That's what twelve-year-old Lil Ant daydreams when his father, Big Ant, is released from prison. Home is Watts, a neighbourhood in Los Angeles right beneath an airport flight path. The relationship between the two is difficult: the boy longs for more affection from his father, who in turn feels Lil Ant should be more manly. That's not easy, as his son likes to walk around with his head in the clouds, drawing inspiration from Greek mythology. One moment he pictures his father as Poseidon, carried by Pegasus, cutting through the sky; the next, Big Ant and his best friend are wandering about in Greek togas. It's this mildly surreal touch that lifts If I Go Will They Miss Me – the second fiction feature from former American journalist Walter Thompson-Hernández – above the average film about a strained parent-child relationship.

imdb.title: If I Go Will They Miss Me
imdb.plot: In Watts, California, a 12-year-old boy attempts to connect with his distant father following his incarceration while sensing mysterious visions, from airplanes and Greek gods, that seem to follow him through his everyday world.

films.title: I Understand Your Displeasure (Ich verstehe Ihren Unmut)
intro: The German social drama I Understand Your Displeasure conveys how working in the cleaning sector is far from spotless. Up close, you experience the hellish workdays alongside the overburdened Heike (an impressive lead performance by 59-year-old debutante Sabine Thalau) as her breathing space shrinks ever further, like a ticking time bomb. Realistic and relevant.
description: Film has the power to reveal what usually remains unseen, including the invisible workforces of society. Heike is one of them. She has been working in the cleaning sector for 40 years. In her role as a manager, mediating daily between the company’s bosses, the clients and the staff, the pressure has increased noticeably. When dark clouds loom, Heike has to get her hands dirty in more ways than one. I Understand Your Displeasure is social realist cinema with a heart for urgent stories in the tradition of the Dardenne brothers and Ken Loach – one need only think of his similarly titled Sorry We Missed You (FFG2019). German director and co-screenwriter Kilian Armando Friedrich makes an empathetic plea for solidarity with this film, which had its world premiere in the Panorama section of the Berlinale. The non-professional lead actress, Sabine Thalau, comes from the sector herself and gives a convincing performance in her very first role.

imdb.title: I Understand Your Displeasure
imdb.plot: A cleaning company manager faces workplace challenges after attempting to recruit from a subcontractor, forcing her to make amends by helping expand their business partnership.

films.title: Isabel
intro: A talented sommelier in São Paulo dreams of opening her own wine bar, away from her controlling boss. In her quest to realise her dream, various paths present themselves: each with its own soundtrack, risks and wonderful vistas. To put it in wine-speak: Isabel is vibrant and fresh film showing great length on the finish.
description: Despite a relatively happy and stable life, Isabel (Marina Person) feels something is missing: a place to serve the natural wines considered too eccentric at the Michelin-starred restaurant where she works as a sommelier. When she decides to open a wine bar in São Paulo, she throws the doors of change wide open. Though driven by passion, Isabel must also contend with the harsh realities of entrepreneurship in a neighbourhood undergoing dramatic change. We watch Isabel battle forces acting on her from both outside and within. "Life isn't perfect, people aren't perfect, but wine mustn't have flaws." Director Gabe Klinger shot his second fiction feature on 16mm to reflect the artisanal character of natural wine. Natural wine lovers will be treated right through to the end of the credits of Isabel.

films.title: Ink
intro: Set against the rise of tabloid journalism, Ink follows Rupert Murdoch and his transformation of the British press. Blending newsroom drama with a nation captivated by scandal, Danny Boyle examines how media power shapes public taste. A stellar cast turns this portrait of influence, ambition and spectacle into compelling cinema.
description: Rupert Murdoch laid the foundations for his media empire in Australia, but the major growth came in the United Kingdom with the acquisition of The Sun in 1969. He turned it into a tabloid, and together with editor Larry Lamb he focused on sensation and sex — such as the Page 3 girl, a full-page photo of a young topless woman. It's all there — along with an infamous kidnapping that caused an uproar in England at the time — in Danny Boyle's Ink (Trainspotting, 1996), with a star cast: Guy Pearce as Murdoch, Jack O'Connell as Lamb, and Claire Foy as a fictional journalist at The Sun. Ink, the opening film of the Venice Film Festival, is a favourite for the Oscars. In the words of Time critic Stephanie Zacharek: "Ink works both as a fictionalised snapshot of a lost world and as a forensic examination of what happens when you give people what they want, rather than what they don't know they want."

imdb.title: Ink
imdb.plot: In 1969, as rising media tycoon acquires the daily newspaper "The Sun," his partnership with editor Larry Lamb turns the paper into Britain's most influential tabloid.

films.title: The Illusion of an Everlasting Summer (La ilusión de un verano sin fin)
intro: Best friends Guille and Beli live on the vast Argentian pampas, where they give free rein to their imagination. For 25 years, photographer Alessandra Sanguinetti followed them—from their lives as a prolonged children’s game to adulthood, which comes with a script of its own. This unique debut film beautifully touches upon the endless summers that live on within us all.
description: Embraced by an open horizon, nine-year-old cousins Guillermina and Belinda tirelessly dream up dance steps while singing of a heartache still unknown to them. For decades, the renowned photographer Alessandra Sanguinetti has been photographing her young neighbours as they are their infectious, uninhibited selves (whether disguised or not). Faced with so much life, video footage joins the photographs. Seasons inevitably blend into one another, and houses, bodies, dreams and friendship take on other forms. Sanguinetti succeeds in capturing something of Guille and Beli's childlike freedom in her images, despite the distances that separate them, words that run dry and grown-up worries. This remarkable documentary, awarded at the Locarno Film Festival, shows the work that goes into a life's work – both in terms of art and the art of living – and the importance of friendship and imagination both in front of and behind the camera.

imdb.title: The Illusion of an Everlasting Summer
imdb.plot: Filmed over twenty-five years, it traces the lives of two inseparable cousins, Guillermina and Belinda, as they grow up in the vast Argentine Pampas.

films.title: Le Journal d'une femme de chambre (Diary of a Chambermaid)
intro: For his French-language debut Diary of a Chambermaid, filmmaker Radu Jude (Bad Luck Banging or Loony Porn) follows freely in the footsteps of Luis Buñuel. With this loose adaptation in his trademark style, the audacious Romanian delivers sharp-witted (meta) commentary on past and present social structures. A timeless classic in a bold new apron.
description: For ten years now, the uncompromising films of Romanian director Radu Jude have been an integral part of Film Fest Gent. Following last year’s Dracula and Kontinental ’25, this edition sees the cultural polymath and absolute speed filmmaker spice things up with his self-proclaimed adaptation of Octave Mirbeau’s famous 19th-century novel Le Journal d’une femme de chambre. Jude sets the story in contemporary France – complete with video calls – and reimagines the maid as a Romanian woman with a daughter far away in her homeland. Combined with a clever meta-structure, this allows the mischievous filmmaker to take a critical look at both the source material and the precarious circumstances of migrant workers. As always, the film is peppered with sharp-witted humour and socio-political jibes that only Jude can get away with. He surrounds the fresh face of lead actress Ana Dumitrașcu with well-known French talent such as Marie Rivière (see the FFG Classics section on Éric Rohmer).

imdb.title: Diary of a Chambermaid
imdb.plot: A young Romanian woman living in France works for a French family and joins a theatre company who are adapting Octave Mirbeau's "The Diary of a Chambermaid."

films.title: Late Fame
intro: Once a promising poet, Ed Saxberger has spent decades sorting mail instead of writing verse. When a group of young artists rediscover his forgotten collection, they hail him as a neglected genius. Willem Dafoe and Greta Lee shine in Kent Jones’ witty, wistful comedy about late fame, artistic vanity and the irresistible desire to finally be seen.
description: Ed Saxberger (Willem Dafoe) has long since put away his dreams of poetry and works as a postal clerk in New York. That is, until a group of young artists rediscover his forgotten collection and promptly proclaim him a misunderstood genius. Ed happily basks in this belated admiration, especially once the eccentric actress Gloria (Greta Lee) crosses his path. Director Kent Jones (Diane, 2018) transplants Arthur Schnitzler's 19th-century novella to present-day New York, working from a screenplay by May December writer Samy Burch. With warmth and gentle mockery, Late Fame pokes fun at artistic egos and the longing to be seen. Dafoe and Lee shine in a delightful game of attraction and appraisal, lending the film both lightness and melancholy. A subtle, wistful comedy about art, vanity and second chances. Because what if you finally get what you once dreamed of – only about forty years too late?

imdb.title: Late Fame
imdb.plot: Legendary New York poet Ed Saxberger's forgotten works captivate an eccentric group of young creatives, reigniting his artistic passion. Their intrigue intertwines with the bewitching presence of actress Gloria.

films.title: The Last Day
intro: The Last Day loosely reimagines Mrs. Dalloway in contemporary America. Julia, a writer who has not written in a decade, feels trapped by marriage and motherhood. Taylor struggles with anxiety and skips a psychiatric appointment. Their lives unfold separately, yet their experiences subtly converge in ways that give the film an emotional resonance.
description: The Last Day is a highly loose adaptation of Virginia Woolf's Mrs. Dalloway. A number of the novel's basic hallmarks are present – a day devoted to errands, the discontented housewife, the unstable stranger, flashes of the past – but the story has been relocated to present-day America on the Fourth of July. The lives of two women are intertwined. Not that they know each other, but their feelings and experiences run strikingly parallel. Julia (Oscar winner Alicia Vikander) is a writer who hasn't put a word on paper in a decade. She's trapped in a none toonhappy marriage and experiences motherhood as a burden. Taylor, meanwhile, tries to keep herself together amid all her anxieties, skipping a planned visit to a psychiatrist. Visual artist Rachel Rose makes her debut with this visually fascinating drama, remarkably paced to the rhythm of a fire engine siren.

imdb.title: The Last Day
imdb.plot: On a July 4th in New York, writer and mother Julia encounters figures from her past and a troubled young mother, prompting her to confront her lack of creative purpose and rediscover herself within the life she has.

films.title: La Libertad Doble (Double Freedom)
intro: Surrounded by the endless pampa, Misael chops wood for a living. For the time being, his days still unfold to a fragile cadence as soothing as the little radio resting on his chest while napping. La Libertad Doble marks both a return to the universe of Alonso’s debut film Libertad (2001) and to the roots of his ever-intruiging craftsmanship.
description: For his seventh film, Argentine filmmaker Lisandro Alonso returned — with the same crew — to the location and protagonist of his debut film, Libertad (2001), where his fascination with the loner first took root. In the quarter of a century separating the two films, Alonso has built an remarkable body of work around solitary men and desolate landscapes. In many respects, the life of lumberjack Misael (Misael Saavedra) has continued much as before. Yet the shockwaves of Milei’s chainsaw-wielding political agenda are sweeping across Argentina at full force, and they will have a profound impact on him too. Even in his most political film to date, Alonso opts for a minimalism that seeps through every layer of the film, delicately captured by Cobi Migliora’s 35mm cinematography. La Libertad Doble (Double Freedom) is a film that breathes freely despite the splinters in the air and the suffocating smoke of roaring chainsaws.

imdb.title: Double Freedom
imdb.plot: Misael lives as an independent logger in the woods, enjoying his solitary freedom. When he must care for his older sister, his peaceful existence is upended and the foundations of his carefully constructed life begin to fall apart.

films.title: Low Expectations (Lave forventninger)
intro: Against all expectations, a breakdown forces a rising music star (Girl in Red singer-songwriter Marie Ulven in her acting debut) to return home. During a seemingly endless summer she tries to come to terms with herself. Norwegian Eivind Landsvik’s first feature Low Expectations premiered in Cannes and captures dark clouds in the mind against bright Scandinavian light.
description: When musician Maja suffers a mental breakdown in a hotel room, she returns to her parents’ home. Under her mother’s wing, the rising star tries to recharge her batteries. Maja takes on a part-time job at a local secondary school, where she cautiously navigates a world full of expectations. Low Expectations marks the feature-length debut of director Eivind Landsvik and lead actress Marie Ulven, known as the singer-songwriter Girl in Red. The film was nominated for the Debut Award at Cannes, following Landsvik’s short film Tits (2023), which had previously been in competition there. His sensitive (visual) style, developed through his experience with music videos, is enhanced by the soft 16mm cinematography. Among the cast, you’ll recognise Anders Danielsen Lie from The Worst Person in the World. Finding his own voice amongst his Norwegian compatriots Joachim Trier and Dag Johan Haugerud (Sex, Dreams, Love), Landsvik carves out his own path.

imdb.title: Low Expectations
imdb.plot: A successful young artist's career derails, forcing her back to her hometown. While teaching high school to make ends meet, she navigates depression and rediscovers herself in unexpected ways.

films.title: The Match
intro: The 1986 World Cup quarter-final between Argentina and England was far more than a football match. Maradona’s infamous “Hand of God” goal made history, but the game also carried the weight of the Falklands War. The Match revisits the fierce rivalry, political tensions and clashes that surrounded the game.
description: During the quarter-final of the 1986 World Cup between Argentina and England, Diego Maradona leapt towards the ball to head it, though he would ultimately flick it over goalkeeper Peter Shilton with his hand. The goal was approved. Maradona later referred to it as “the Hand of God”. Argentina won the match and went on to win the World Cup. Much has been written and debated about that incident, and The Match (El partido) is now the definitive documentary on this fixture. For even without the ‘Hand of God’ moment, this was a particularly memorable match: the first encounter between the two nations since Argentina had invaded the Falklands four years earlier and subsequently lost that war. Long before kick-off, the tension in the stadium was palpable, whilst clashes broke out between the two sets of supporters in the streets of Mexico City. One more thing: the ball was auctioned off last August for 2.9 million euros.

imdb.title: The Match
imdb.plot: Follows the 1986 Argentina-England World Cup quarter final, exploring how the match became a culmination of tensions between the two nations following the 1982 Falklands War.

films.title: Meine Frau weint (My Wife Cries)
intro: In Meine Frau weint (My Wife Cries), Angela Schanelec follows crane operator Thomas after he learns that his wife Sonja’s dance partner has died. The event transforms their relationship and reveals hidden tensions. Through restrained performances, precise dialogue and carefully observed moments, the film explores love, guilt and the fragile limits of human connection.
description: The opening shot alone makes My Wife Cries an absolute must-see. For eight minutes, we watch crane operator Thomas as he fiddles with his phone and talks to other characters who remain out of the camera’s view. Fortunately, what follows is just as worthwhile. Thomas is called to his inconsolable wife, Sonja. Bit by bit, she tells him that her dance partner has been killed in an accident. It is then that it begins to dawn on Thomas. German director Angela Schanelec steers well clear of melodrama. With plenty of silences and a keen sense of nuance, she explores the relationship between Thomas and Sonja: love, guilt and the inability to truly connect with another person are key themes. And whilst there’s quite a lot of talking, how much is actually being said? Because language often seems to fall short. A restrained, yet no less moving, relationship drama featuring a surprising cameo for Leonard Cohen’s “Lover, Lover, Lover”.

imdb.title: My Wife Cries
imdb.plot: During his construction shift, crane operator Thomas, 40, gets a call to pick up his wife from the hospital. He finds her alone and weeping on a bench outside.

films.title: Memory
intro: In the deeply personal, poetic documentary Memory, Crimea-born filmmaker Vladlena Sandu seeks to deal with the war trauma from her Chechen childhood. She longs to transform fear into love using the power of imagination as her weapon, rooted in her memories and directed towards a future for children. A haunting, evocative and almost mythical feature-length debut.
description: Born in Crimea, Vladlena Sandu was sent to live with her grandparents in Grozny, Chechnya at a young age. There, in 1994, following the collapse of the Soviet Union, she became caught up in Russia's occupying war against the Chechen people. Aggression engulfed the city and her family. With her autobiographical feature debut Memory, the director bravely returns to the traumatic memories of her childhood. The film opened Giornate degli Autori, an independent section of the Venice Film Festival. Through an imaginative visual language inspired by the work of Sergei Parajanov and Andrei Tarkovsky, Sandu seeks an answer to the fundamental question of how to break the cycle of violence – before it shapes the next generation of children. Innocence is poetically contrasted with loss across a series of poignant and intimate tableaux. What role can art play in the healing process? Despite everything, Sandu remains hopeful.

films.title: Moscas (Flies)
intro: In Moscas, Mexican director Fernando Eimbcke tells the story of Olga, who rents out a room to a father and his nine-year-old son Christian while the father spends time with his hospitalised wife. As Olga and Christian grow closer, the film explores connection, loss and vulnerability through quiet observation, subtle humor and retro video games.
description: With Moscas – Spanish for ‘flies’ – Mexican director Fernando Eimbcke returns to the black-and-white aesthetic and soothing minimalism of his finest film, Temporada de patos. In need of money, Olga rents out a room in her flat to a man and his nine-year-old son, Christian, whose wife/mother is in a nearby hospital. As the father spends a lot of time with his wife, Olga and Christian end up spending a lot of time together. Eimbcke has always had a knack for young actors, but Bastian Escobar as Christian is a real discovery. Essentially, Moscas tackles heavy themes such as (the fear of) connection and loss, but Eimbcke’s observational approach – with mostly static shots – and the flashes of humour that bubble up from everyday actions serve to soften the blow. And there’s another surprising element that tempers the intensity: the presence of old-school video games. How and why? It would be a shame to give away before you see the film.

imdb.title: Flies
imdb.plot: When Olga has to rent out a room in her apartment to a father, she forms an unlikely bond with his nine-year old son when, unexpectedly, their lives become intertwined.

films.title: Nowhere to Lay My Eyes
intro: After ten years, Sanghee returns to the South Korean island of Jeju with her brother to visit their mother, whose restaurant has unexpectedly become a success. As they spend time together, old expectations, unsolicited advice and unspoken feelings rise to the surface.
description: Hong Sang-soo, by now the director, screenwriter, producer, cinematographer, editor and sound recordist of his own films, is back as if he never left. Kim Min-hee plays a young experimental filmmaker who returns to visit her mother after years away, for a weekend that turns out to be cosy, awkward and painful in equal measure. Her mother would love nothing more than for her daughter to move closer to her, but that wish proves less straightforward than she had hoped. Beneath the everyday conversations lie loneliness, regret and a longing for connection. Hong swaps his familiar pianos and synths for a lo-fi, ominous post-punk guitar à la Slint, and occasionally lets Kim Min-hee narrate in voice-over. But as always, the subtle humour lies in the details: a coffee shop playing Satie, a monologue about a morbid burial ritual, and grilled prawns. It is Hong at his best: small in gesture, big in feeling and irresistibly human.

imdb.title: Nowhere to Lay My Eyes
imdb.plot: Follows Sanghee as she visits her mother on Jeju Island after 10 years, reuniting with her brother and meeting her stepfather and his daughter while navigating family dynamics and personal pursuits.

films.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
intro: As cash disappears, so do opportunities for old-school pickpockets. Harry Lehman, a principled New York thief with a heart of gold, steals a bag belonging to a crime family heir and unknowingly takes a USB drive. After selling it, he must get it back before his wife Rosie pays the price. A tense, bittersweet thriller in which every New York street grows more dangerous and time ever scarcer.
description: The fact that we're using less and less cash also has unexpected consequences. Because what's a seasoned pickpocket, who can nimbly snatch a wallet from someone's coat or handbag, meant to do? Harry Lehman, the main character of The Only Living Pickpocket in New York, knows all about it. He's a pickpocket with principles and a heart of gold; almost a Robin Hood. When he steals a holdall from the crown prince of a crime family, he lands himself in trouble. Not because of the guns or the eye-wateringly expensive watch, but because of a USB stick that Harry very quickly offloads. Unfortunately, the family need the USB stick back. If he fails, his wife Rosie will pay the price with a heap of misery. This thriller becomes a race against time, with a wistful undertone that also serves as a portrait of New York City. John Turturro delivers one of his very best performances yet here.

imdb.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
imdb.plot: When a theft goes awry, a veteran pickpocket is sent on a mission through New York to reclaim it.

films.title: Remake
intro: American documentarian Ross McElwee had been filming his family for decades when his son Adrian unexpectedly passed away in 2016. Dedicated and addressed to Adrian, Remake looks back on their complex relationship through footage shot by both of them, with McElwee questioning his closely intertwined role as a filmmaker and father. Heart-wrenching and deeply personal.
description: "The story I thought I was telling through my films, the stories of lives unfolding over decades, is now incoherent and confusing." American documentary maker Ross McElwee is celebrated for autobiographical work that closely involves his family, but after the death of his troubled son Adrian, he put down the camera for years. Remake is his attempt to pick up the thread again. McElwee confronts the many images at his disposal (unused archive footage, material from previous films, or footage shot by his son himself), all while wrestling with his dual role as filmmaker and father. Meanwhile, a Hollywood producer wants to adapt his influential Sherman's March (1986), for which McElwee was once accused: "This is not art, this is life!" With Remake, he tries to reconcile the two. The result is emotionally devastating and multifaceted. The film was awarded the Golden Globe Impact Prize for Documentary in Venice.

imdb.title: Remake
imdb.plot: Ross McElwee explores time and memory through footage of his son Adrian, weaving their shared filmmaking past with an unfinished Hollywood remake of Sherman's March, creating a meditation on loss and documentation.

films.title: The Other Side of the Sun
intro: From the shadows of Syria’s infamous Sednaya prison, five survivors return to the place where years of their lives were stolen. Through powerful re-enactments, Tawfik Sabouni explores memory, trauma and the struggle to reclaim silenced voices, revealing how human connection can endure even in a place built on fear and destruction.
description: Years after filmmaker Tawfik Sabouni was released from Sednaya, the Syrian prison that became a symbol of oppression under the Assad regime, he returns to the place of his imprisonment. Together with four other survivors, he confronts the corridors, cells and walls that have scarred their lives. Not to reopen the trauma, but to give space to memories that were suppressed for years. By carefully reconstructing scenes from their imprisonment, the men bring daily rituals and moments of survival back to life. The empty cells become a twilight zone between life and death. With his sober, understated style, Sabouni shows how fear and the impossibility of forgetting coexist with stories, solidarity and tenderness. The Other Side of the Sun is not only a testimony from these five men, but also a reminder of the countless voices that were lost.

screenings.guests: Tawfik Sabouni (Director, Screenplay, Cast), Dani Abo Louh (Editor), Julie Freres (Producer), Hanne Phlypo (Co-Producer, Contact person)

imdb.title: The Other Side of the Sun
imdb.plot: After the fall of Assad's regime, five survivors return to the former torture prison of Saidnaya to reenact what they experienced there. They reclaim their voices and bear witness for those who can no longer speak for themselves.

films.title: Salvation (Kurtuluş)
intro: In a remote Turkish mountain village, a land dispute between two rival clans spirals into violence. In Salvation, director Emin Alper slowly blurs the line between dream and reality, turning a local conflict into a powerful parable about power, religious fervour, rumours and collective paranoia. Winner of the Silver Bear Grand Jury Prize at Berlin film festival.
description: Two clans stand facing each other, knives drawn, in a remote Turkish mountain village. The Hazerans have successfully defended the village against a terrorist attack, whilst the Bezaris fled. Now that calm has returned, the latter want their land back, leading to an ever-escalating spiral of violence. In Salvation (Kurtuluş), director Emin Alper slowly builds the tension and allows the boundary between dream and reality to fade imperceptibly. This story of a local dispute evolves into a universal parable about power. Rumours, religious visions and collective paranoia create a reality of their own in which fanaticism flares up. The soundtrack by Dutch composer Christiaan Verbeek heightens the sense of foreboding. Awarded the 'Große Preis der Jury' – the second prize, you could say – at the Berlin Film Festival, Salvation confirms that Alper is one of the most original voices in contemporary Turkish cinema.

imdb.title: Salvation
imdb.plot: A sheikh faces a territorial dispute when a rival tribe returns to reclaim their ancestral land. He and his brother clash over how to handle the escalating conflict following a period of regional violence.

films.title: Sete anos em Maio (Seven Years in May)
intro: This film is part of Seven Years in May / Disciplina, a collection of two mid-length films directed by Affonso Uchôa.
description: In a night in May, seven years ago, Rafael arrived home from work. When he was opening the gate, someone called his name. He looked back and saw people he didn't know. Rafael left his house carried by the unknown people and never came back. Since then he lives as if that night has never ended.

parts.title: Sete anos em Maio (Seven Years in May)

imdb.title: Seven Years in May
imdb.plot: A man, whose character is based on that of the actor who plays him, contemplates the time he was brutalized by a gang of fake cops into revealing where in his house he had stashed some drugs, which he denied having.

films.title: Siempre soy tu animal materno (Forever Your Maternal Animal)
intro: In her sophomore film Costa Rican director Valentina Maurel paints a vivid portrait of an eccentric family and their profusion of uncertain desires, ambiguous intentions and an overarching need for change. Here, reaching adulthood does not mark the end of the process of growing up, but rather its messy and equally painful and fascinating continuation.
description: Back in Costa Rica (temporarily), Elsa (Daniela Marín) finds herself caught up in the family dynamics she had left behind. Whilst her mother is reclaiming time for herself now that her daughters have grown up, her father is seeking to reinvent himself through a new romance. Elsa’s sister Amalia seeks stability in uncertain circumstances and hopes that her sister’s return will herald better times. Elsa takes on the responsibility, but is searching for her own path. In Valentina Maurel’s work, mothers, fathers, daughters and sisters are never reduced to merely those roles. They are rebels, poets, lovers, travellers… In her debut film (with an equally delightful poetic title), Tengo sueños eléctricos (I Have Electric Dreams) (2022), Maurel already explored the complexity of family ties. Her second film remains true to that spirit and won an award for best acting at Cannes.

imdb.title: Forever Your Maternal Animal
imdb.plot: Elsa, 28, returns to Costa Rica from Europe and reconnects with her sister Amalia, 20, who's on an esoteric, existential path. Their father Nahuel pursues romantic conquests while mother Isabel republishes her erotic poems.

films.title: Soudain (All of a Sudden)
intro: After acclaimed films such as Evil Does Not Exist, Ryūsuke Hamaguchi moves his camera to France for the first time. Virginie Efira plays a care home director whose understanding of dignity is transformed by meeting a seriously ill Japanese playwright. Through patient observation, silences and conversations, Hamaguchi explores chance, fate and life-changing encounters.
description: Following a series of critically acclaimed films (Evil Does Not Exist, Drive My Car) set in his homeland Japan, director Ryūsuke Hamaguchi sets his camera for the first time in France. Virginie Efira plays the director of a care home who, despite staff shortages and almost insurmountable bureaucracy, wants to offer the residents as dignified a life (and end of life) as possible, following an approach she has developed herself: ‘humanitude’. But her view of care changes radically following an encounter with a seriously ill Japanese playwright. Hamaguchi’s camera patiently observes their relationship – through long conversations, telling silences and subtle gestures. As is often the case with Hamaguchi, chance and fate perform a courtship dance. At over three hours long, Soudain is a long sit, but this moving film about chance, vulnerability and unexpected encounters that can change a life is well worth your time.

imdb.title: All of a Sudden
imdb.plot: Marie-Lou runs a nursing home near Paris and strives for more humane elder care. Her friendship with Mari, a Japanese theatre director facing terminal cancer, deepens her commitment to residents' dignity.

films.title: Strawberries (La más dulce)
intro: Sweet fruit soon takes on a bitter taste in this powerful indictment of exploitation on Spanish strawberry farms. We follow the arduous journey of a combative Moroccan woman who migrated to Spain hoping for a fresh start. Together with colleagues she starts a protest that takes her from the fields all the way to the courtroom. A moving portrait of sisterhood.
description: In the vegetable garden of Europe, Hasna (Nisrin Erradi) works for the strawberry farm ‘La más dulce’ (‘the sweetest’). Along with other Moroccan women, she is forced to pick strawberries non-stop in overheated plastic greenhouses. To comply with the imposed orders, the women, constantly urged on and with bent backs, must work themselves to the bone day after day. Knowing full well that they have only each other to fall back on, a sisterhood develops that will prove to be of vital importance. As an acclaimed taekwondo practitioner, Hasna is combative, even though she is also battling ghosts from her own past. Filmmaker Laïla Marrakchi portrays the struggle of women who must function within a dark system that thrives entirely on exploitation. Their resilience and mutual solidarity takes center stage. Marrakchi delivers a film that resonates and after which strawberries will never taste the same again.

imdb.title: Strawberries
imdb.plot: Two young women leave their native Morocco to work a season picking strawberries in Spain, until abuse and harassment shatter their hopes. Supported by a Spanish lawyer, they must decide whether to speak out against a powerful system.

films.title: Violence du corps de l’autre (Nobody's Violence)
intro: Mira crosses Canada helping people end their lives, a job that leaves her increasingly isolated. Her encounter with Flanagan, an enigmatic young man, unsettles her routine when he starts appearing near her clients. Denis Côté turns this portrait of a troubled woman into an eerie, elusive thriller, shot on grainy 16mm, where mood and tension linger.
description: Mira travels across Canada helping people end their lives. It's a solitary existence that, we gradually discover, weighs on her more than it first appears. Until she meets a mysterious man, Flanagan (Xavier Bergeron, who received a special mention at the Locarno Film Festival for his performance). He draws her out of her emotional isolation. However, his presence starts to become unsettling as he keeps turning up near her patients. Canadian director Denis Côté (Paul, FFG25) stays well off the beaten track. Violence du corps de l'autre is the portrait of a remarkable woman, raises questions about assisted suicide, and evolves into a sibylline thriller. Shot on grainy 16mm, this fiction film relies more on atmosphere and emotion than on a clearly defined story. That's no bad thing, as Côté conjures images that linger long in the mind.

imdb.title: Nobody's Violence
imdb.plot: Follows a travelling girl offering euthanasia services in a dystopian world.

films.title: The Uprising
intro: After the devastating plague epidemic, an English farmer refuses to accept the taxes he can no longer afford to pay. His resistance grows into a revolt that threatens to throw the entire country into turmoil. With Paul Greengrass, the director of the Jason Bourne trilogy, at the helm, you can expect plenty of hard-hitting action.
description: Andrew Garfield plays an impoverished farmer with disarming simplicity who, after the plague epidemic has wiped out more than half the population, can no longer afford to pay his taxes. His resistance to King Richard II inadvertently sparks a popular revolt, as farmers and workers unite against a system that continues to exploit them ever harder. Paul Greengrass, master of the shaky cam and the Jason Bourne trilogy, brings this true story, which helped lay the foundations for the legend of Robin Hood, to the screen with raw intensity and momentum. The Uprising is about injustice and class inequality, but also about the thin line between resistance and blind collective rage. Once an angry mob is set in motion, it is difficult to predict where it will end – an unsettling echo of the storming of the US Capitol on January 6. With large-scale battle scenes and Greengrass’s nervous camerawork, medieval history suddenly feels startlingly relevant.

imdb.title: The Uprising
imdb.plot: Based on the true story of the uprising that inspired the legend of Robin Hood, Andrew Garfield stars as the leader of a rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II in a fight for justice.

films.title: The Weight
intro: Padraic McKinley’s gripping debut throws Ethan Hawke into a brutal fight for freedom. In 1933, convict Samuel Murphy must smuggle a fortune in gold through unforgiving wilderness to escape prison and save his young daughter from adoption. With a handpicked crew, he faces a nerve-shredding ordeal of distrust, betrayal, violence and exhaustion.
description: The 1970s are back in full force in The Weight, a raw, gripping survival thriller that grabs you by the throat from the very first minutes. For his debut film, director Padraic McKinkley drew inspiration from 1970s classics such as Deliverance and Sorcerer. In 1933, during the Great Depression, Samuel Murphy (Ethan Hawke) is separated from his young daughter Penny and sent to a ruthless penal camp. A guard (Russell Crowe) promises to help Murphy escape in exchange for smuggling a hoard of gold across an inhospitable wasteland. Time is running out, as Penny is about to be given up for adoption. With a few accomplices of his own choosing, Murphy embarks on a nerve-wracking journey that can be summed up in four key words: mistrust, betrayal, violence and exhaustion. A truly brilliant Hawke commands the audience’s attention for two hours. His weathered face is a perfect fit for this thrilling adventure film.

imdb.title: The Weight
imdb.plot: Desperate to save what is left of his family, during the height of the Great Depression, a battle-scarred veteran is hired to help smuggle a fortune in gold across 100 miles of impenetrable wilderness.

films.title: Why Do I See You In Everything?
intro: Resisting all types of easy categorisation, Syrian director Rand Abou Fakher’s full length feature debut Why Do I See You In Everything? is a disorienting hybrid documentary that contrasts violence with tenderness, and displacement with belonging. A poetic plaint that proves home truly is where the heart is, by focusing on the shared history of two lifelong friends.
description: A convoy of trucks winds its way through the desert, fully grown trees swaying precariously in their beds. The opening shot of Why Do I See You In Everything? seems almost randomly chosen, just one of the many snapshots that protagonists Nabil and Qusay managed to capture during their protests in Syria. Gradually, however, it becomes clear that the felled greenery serves as a metaphor for uprooting, land grabbing and violence. In this hybrid documentary, Syrian director Rand Abou Fakher closely follows the journey of two childhood friends. For decades, Nabil and Qusay make their way through political unrest, from Syria to Berlin, camera in hand. Archive footage and staged scenes alternate throughout this blend of documentary and fiction. The result is an associative collage with which Fakher fires off a sharp political statement at the viewer. Not just loud protest, but also friendship, intimacy and care are radical forms of resistance.

screenings.guests: Hans Bruch (Camera (DOP)), Rand Abou Fakher (Director, Screenplay, Producer, Editor), Nabil Altawil (Cast), Qusay Awad (Screenplay, Cast), Rosa Galguera Ortega (Applicant, Producer)

imdb.title: Why Do I See You in Everything?
imdb.plot: Two Syrian friends in Berlin navigate memories, footage and current events, examining political violence while affirming love and care as acts of resistance.

films.title: Wild Horse Nine
intro: Two CIA agents arrive on Easter Island for an apparently innocent assignment, only to be confronted with their past. In this offbeat buddy comedy by Martin McDonagh, a tropical getaway spirals into an absurdist trip filled with dark humour and paranoia.
description: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are sent to Easter Island by their boss for a mandatory vacation. Amid the mysterious moai and paradisiacal landscapes, their getaway descends into paranoia and a confrontation with their past. Following Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri (FFG2017) and The Banshees of Inisherin (FFG2022), Martin McDonagh continues to build on his trademark style of razor-sharp dialogue, dark humour and clashing characters. But beneath the absurdity lies a more serious story: one about guilt, accountability and the question of how to come to terms with yourself and a dark national history. As the ageing Chris, John Malkovich gives a performance that is at once dryly comic and surprisingly vulnerable - rarely has he been so moving.

imdb.title: Wild Horse Nine
imdb.plot: CIA agents Chris and Lee face a trust-testing mission from Santiago to Easter Island during 1973 in Chile.

films.title: Yesterday the Eye Didn't Sleep
intro: In a village on the border between Lebanon and Syria, two women are forced to leave their home to help quell a blood feud in their community. They face an uncertain future, shaped by a legacy of revenge. This lyrical debut film, shot without a script and with a cast of untrained actors, incisively explores the role of women in times of tension and unspoken conflict.
description: A burnt-out lorry and a fatal accident threaten to set off a spiral of violence within the Bedouin community in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley. Within the accused family, sisters Rim (Rim Al Mawla) and Jawaher (Jawaher Al Mawla), each with a very different temperament, must pay the price with their freedom. Palestinian filmmaker Rakan Mayasi shot his debut feature without a traditional script and with a cast of untrained actors. Thanks to Pôl Seif's beautiful cinematography, Mayasi steeps his film in rich observations of the mountain landscape, the atmosphere and the rituals within the shepherding community. Yesterday the Eye Didn't Sleep poetically explores what unfolds in the silence, between the fields, behind the curtains, in delivery vans. It is about women carrying too much with them, men speaking in codes, a country holding its breath, unable to find sleep.

screenings.guests: Jennifer Ritter (Producer), Rakan Mayasi (Director, Screenplay, Producer), Louis De Schrijver (Editor)

imdb.title: Yesterday the Eye Didn't Sleep
imdb.plot: In a valley shrouded in fog and tribal codes, two sisters go into the night as an offering. Between blood, memories and silences, they try to contain the fire that threatens to spread.

films.title: Wildwood
intro: After her brother vanishes into the clutches of mysterious crows, Prue and classmate Curtis venture beyond Portland into Wildwood, a secret realm of magic, talking creatures and lurking threats. Their search collides with a ruler destroyed by grief. A dark fantasy turned into a visually dazzling adventure stop-motion animated film.
description: When Mac, Prue McKeel’s younger brother, is kidnapped by a murder of crows, she refuses to sit idly by. Together with her somewhat clumsy classmate Curtis, she ventures into the forbidden forest outside Portland to search for Mac. Their journey soon proves to be far more complex than a simple rescue mission. Wildwood is a hidden world full of talking animals, people with magical powers and dangerous enemies. The Dowager Alexandra once ruled the forest benevolently. But, caught in a downward spiral of grief, she has succumbed to evil. This heightens the danger for Prue and Curtis. Laika, the studio behind stop-motion animation gems such as Coraline and Kubo and the Two Strings, delivers another smash hit with Wildwood, backed by a brilliant star-studded cast (Carey Mulligan, Awkwafina, Tom Waits, and others). An animated film for adults and older children, though not suitable for the very youngest.

imdb.title: Wildwood
imdb.plot: The adventures of Prue McKeel as she sets off to the forests outside Portland to find her kidnapped brother.

films.title: La vie rêvée (Dream Life)
intro: Videodroom welcomes Icelandic experimental pop pioneers múm for a brand-new live soundtrack to the tranquil Canadian cult classic La vie rêvée (Dream Life). On stage, they will be joined by their close friend, composer and cellist Hildur Guðnadóttir.
description: When Isabelle (Liliane Lemaître-Auger) starts working at a local film production company, she befriends the animator Virginie (Véronique Le Flaguais). During a sunny summer in Montréal, the two young women find their way through love, work, politics and the endless search for the ideal partner. Gradually, they discover that reality rarely lives up to their dreams. La vie rêvée is a tender portrait of female friendship and youthful ideals.Rather than telling a conventional story, director Mireille Dansereau captures a time and a place with exceptional warmth and intimacy. The grainy 16mm footage gives the film the feel of an intimate home movie, whilst the playful, collage-like editing constantly shifts between dream and reality. Often compared to the work of Agnès Varda, La vie rêvée is both a milestone in Canadian cinema – the first feature film directed by a woman in Québec – and a hidden gem waiting to be rediscovered.

Few bands capture the film’s dreamy atmosphere quite as well as múm. Since their formation in Reykjavík in the late 1990s, the ever-evolving collective has built a unique musical universe in which gentle melodies, delicate vocals, glitch electronica, field recordings and acoustic instruments blend seamlessly. With eight acclaimed albums, countless collaborations and music for film and theatre, múm have become one of Iceland’s most important and beloved bands.For this special performance, the group will be joined by the acclaimed composer and cellist Hildur Guðnadóttir, who has maintained a close artistic relationship with múm since their early years. Guðnadóttir has since become one of the leading film composers of her generation, having won an Oscar, a Grammy, a Golden Globe and an Emmy for her music for Joker and Chernobyl, alongside highly acclaimed soundtracks for films such as TÁR and Sicario: Day of the Soldado.Exclusively for Videodroom, múm and Hildur Guðnadóttir bring this extraordinary film to life with a completely new live soundtrack.

imdb.title: Dream Life
imdb.plot: Two twenty-something women dream of the ideal man and slowly realize that reality is very different from their fantasies.

films.title: Spider Baby or, The Maddest Story Ever Told
intro: We present a unique screening of pitch-black horror comedy Spider Baby, where legendary avant-noise duo Wolf Eyes takes on the soundtrack of this camp classic.

Spider Baby—also known as Cannibal Orgy and The Maddest Story Ever Told—from 1967 is a bizarre piece of exploitation cinema. Too intense to be a true comedy but too 'cutesy' to be pure horror, it hovers somewhere between The Addams Family and The Texas Chainsaw Massacre. A cartoonish slice of grindhouse that revels in its own contrarian nature and twisted anarchy.
description: In a dilapidated mansion, the last descendants of the Merrye family live in complete anarchy. Due to a genetic disease, they have regressed into a childlike state, giving in to cannibalism and homicidal urges. The youngest daughter, Virginia (Jill Banner), believes she is a human spider and creeps through the house looking for prey. Meanwhile, the eldest son, Ralphie (played by cult actor Sid Haig), hunts stray cats to serve for dinner. The orphans are cared for (and kept in check) by chauffeur and butler Bruno (a brilliant role for horror icon Lon Chaney Jr.). When a few distant relatives and their lawyer unexpectedly visit with their eyes on the inheritance, all hell—naturally—breaks loose.

Spider Baby is the brainchild of cult director Jack Hill—famous for blaxploitation and camp classics like Coffy, Foxy Brown, and Switchblade Sisters, and affectionately described by Quentin Tarantino as 'the Howard Hawks of exploitation cinema'.
Who else but Wolf Eyes would want to provide this film with a brand-new score?

Wolf Eyes (John Olson and Nate Young) formed in Michigan in 1998 and are known for their unique & uncompromising sound: putting noise, industrial, free jazz, and avant-garde into a blender, resulting in hypnotic and unpredictable performances that are intense from start to finish. With countless releases on vinyl, CDR, and cassette, they are one of the most active and inspiring experimental acts of the past 25 years.

parts.title: Spider Baby or, The Maddest Story Ever Told

imdb.title: Spider Baby or, The Maddest Story Ever Told
imdb.plot: A household of cannibals take drastic measures when distant relatives question their sanity.

films.title: The Street Fighter
intro: The relentless cinematic violence of The Street Fighter meets the pounding percussion and raw noise of NAH. His brand-new live soundtrack catapults the grindhouse classic The Street Fighter (1974) straight into the 21st century. A martial arts extravaganza guaranteed.
description: The Streetfighter is notorious. It was the first film ever to receive an X-rating in the US solely for its intense violence and gore. At the same time, it marked the absolute breakthrough for legendary Japanese martial artist Sonny Chiba. The film spawned two direct sequels and laid the groundwork for the iconic arcade game of the same name.

Riding the wave of Bruce Lee’s Enter The Dragon, the so-called "exploitation" and "grindhouse" cinema had reached its absolute peak. The world was ready for Chiba’s raw brand of action. Yet, Chiba was no cheap Bruce Lee clone looking to cash in on a trend. Where Lee shines in elegance and Jackie Chan excels in comic playfulness, Chiba rules with pure, unrestrained, barbaric fury. The moment his character Terry Tsurugi cuts loose, nobody is safe—neither his enemies nor the bystanders. When another character calls him "an animal" mid-film, Chiba, snarling and growling, does absolutely nothing to contradict her.

It is exactly this ruthless ferocity that cemented the film’s cult status. Think of scenes where Chiba castrates a rapist with his bare hands, or where a single blow cuts directly to an X-ray shot of a shattering skull before the opponent collapses, blood gushing from his mouth. The tone is set.

The plot? A textbook cocktail of honor, revenge, and betrayal, settled entirely with fists and feet. Chiba plays Terry Tsurugi: a cynical assassin-for-hire who cares only for sex, money, and fighting. He is hired to break a condemned martial arts master out of prison. When his demands for a higher fee are denied, he coldly abandons the job. But after the Yakuza and the Hong Kong mafia kidnap the condemned man's sister, Tsurugi gets dragged into a bloody gang war anyway.
About NAH
The heavy task of providing this skull-crushing action classic with a fresh live score belongs to an artist whose love for obscure horror and B-movies bleeds through every single track.

NAH (aka Michul Kuun) is a Philadelphia-born, Antwerp-based percussionist, producer, and visual artist. Since dropping his first demos in 2011, he has been carving out his own hyper-dynamic sound from textured noise and genre-smashing percussive rhythms. His roots? Deeply planted in DIY punk, noise, avant-jazz, electronics, and the restless urgency of hip-hop.Armed with little more than a drum kit and an arsenal of samplers, he channels a frenetic live energy that teeters on the razor-thin edge of raw aggression and playful chaos. In recent years, alongside producing his own work, he has collaborated with heavyweights like Wiki, MIKE, Moor Mother, Iggor Cavalera, Evicshen, Cities Aviv, and Obongjayar.

imdb.title: The Street Fighter
imdb.plot: After failing to reach a deal with her enemies, a mercenary karate master protects the daughter of a recently-deceased oil tycoon from the evil conglomerate gunning for her inheritance.

films.title: Victorian Psycho
intro: In 1858, Winifred Notty arrives at Ensor House as governess to two precocious children. Her polished manners hide a gruesome appetite and a trail of dead bodies. Maika Monroe plays her with wicked delight, while the movie mixes gore, black comedy and gothic unease. The result is a playful horror flick where the Victorian facade cracks before us.
description: It is 1858 in Victorian England, an era in which a dark truth often lurks behind a respectable façade. The eccentric Winifred Notty arrives at Ensor House, a remote estate where she becomes governess to the two precocious children of the household. She behaves impeccably, but she also displays some disturbing impulses. Early in the film, she finds an ear in her bedroom, which she devours with great relish. In voice-over, she reveals that she has left a trail of dead bodies in her wake as a governess. Her home village is notorious for its many dead babies. In short, as a viewer you soon know exactly what you're dealing with. Scream queen Maika Monroe (It Follows, Longlegs) portrays her with devilish relish. The (dark) humour is at least as important in Victorian Psycho as the horror, though director Zachary Wigon (Sanctuary) also delivers a fair dose of gore.

For over a decade, the Ghent-based film collective Kuru has been sharing its love for horror and cult cinema through special screenings and themed events. Every screening is unique and delightfully offbeat. At the premiere of Victorian Psycho on October 14th, Kuru will get the audience in the mood with a group session of ‘kuruoke’ – their twisted take on karaoke.

imdb.plot: In 1858, an eccentric young governess, Winifred Notty, arrives at the remote gothic manor Ensor House. As Winifred assimilates, staff begin to inexplicably disappear, and the owners wonder if something is amiss about this new governess.

films.title: Outrage
intro: In Outrage director Ida Lupino tackles a sexual assault and its aftermath in a - for the time - groundbreaking and taboo shattering way. This underseen and devastatingly beautiful noir gets a brand new score by composer and electronic artist Laryssa Kim.
description: Ida Lupino: A Cinema Pioneer

Lupino described herself as a “bulldozer” when finding project finances, but a “mother” on set, nurturing her actors. She was a cinema pioneer, especially in telling women’s stories. After starting as an actor (starring opposite Humphrey Bogart in High Sierra), she became the first woman to direct a film noir (The Hitch-Hiker, 1953) and the only woman to direct an episode of The Twilight Zone. In her eight films, she fearlessly tackled controversial subjects like unplanned pregnancy (Not Wanted, 1949) and bigamy (The Bigamist).

Her crowning achievement is Outrage (1950). By depicting sexual assault, Lupino challenged classical Hollywood cinema and strict Hays Code censorship. The film follows Ann Walton (Mala Powers), who, after being attacked by a stranger, is unable to continue her normal life and runs away. Although the word 'rape' is never used, the film’s frankness about trauma and debilitating flashbacks (PTSD) was decades ahead of its time. Breaking with the victim-blaming attitudes of the era, Lupino portrays Ann with pure empathy, creating a pioneering piece of feminist filmmaking that still impacts contemporary viewers.
The Live Score: Laryssa Kim

The newly composed soundtrack is in the capable hands of multifaceted Italo-Congolese artist Laryssa Kim. Her ritual-like dreamscapes, where musique concrète melds with ambient electronics and tender vocals, have been making waves recently—with her mesmerizing album Contezza praised by Pitchfork last year.

Born in Rome, Kim refined her craft within Amsterdam’s contemporary dance and physical theatre circles before making Brussels her creative home in 2013. There, she earned a Master’s in Acousmatic Composition. On stage, her soulful voice floats over hypnotic soundscapes, field recordings, bare-bones trip-hop textures, and shape-shifting electroacoustic arrangements. In this oneiric realm, Laryssa Kim leads listeners into an immersive, trance-like sound odyssey.

imdb.title: Outrage
imdb.plot: A young woman who has just become engaged has her life completely shattered when she is raped while on her way home from work.

films.title: Dead Man
intro: For many cinephiles, Dead Man is director Jim Jarmusch's crowning achievement; a spiritual and poetic Western that radically turns the genre inside out. Especially for Videodroom, Ghent-based guitarist Filip Wauters transforms Dead Man’s iconic guitar soundtrack (by the one and only Neil Young) into a spellbinding steel guitar performance.
description: After a brawl spirals out of control, young accountant William Blake (Johnny Depp) goes on the run. He crosses paths with an enigmatic Native American named 'Nobody' (Gary Farmer), who takes him on a journey through a surreal and violent Wild West.

Like many films featured at VIDEODROOM, this unpredictable and idiosyncratic black-and-white Western wasn’t an instant box office hit when it was released in 1996. Over time, however, it grew into a true cult phenomenon—largely thanks to Neil Young's legendary soundtrack. Young improvised the score entirely on electric guitar, live on the spot, while watching the film for the very first time. The vast, sweeping melodies he conjured up are, as always, dripping with feedback and melancholy.

Starring Johnny Depp alongside a stellar supporting cast featuring the likes of Robert Mitchum, Crispin Glover, John Hurt, Gabriel Byrne, Lance Henriksen, Billy Bob Thornton, Alfred Molina, and Iggy Pop, Dead Man is a one-of-a-kind anti-Western. Jim Jarmusch remains one of America’s most celebrated indie directors, with classics such as Down By Law, Mystery Train, Broken Flowers, and Only Lovers Left Alive to his name.
About Filip Wauters

Ghent guitarist Filip Wauters boasts an extensive track record across various musical projects, including BackBack, Spook, and The Whodads. Armed with his Fender Dual Professional Console steel guitar, he reinterprets Neil Young’s original score in his own distinctive style.

films.title: Maddie's Secret
intro: A dishwasher goes viral as a trendy food influencer, but the fairy tale has a dark side to it. Versatile queer and alt comedian John Early steals the show as the female lead in his directorial debut. Completely unironic and defying categorisation, Maddie’s Secret unapologetically celebrates ‘bad taste’ melodramas. As dead serious as it is deadly funny and sincere.
description: Two-time Emmy-nominated gay cult comedian John Early has built up a loyal fanbase in his home country of America over many years. Early's performances, including covers of pop divas, are shot through with sincere gender-bending and a love of the exaggerated emotions and aesthetics of camp (aimed squarely against 'good' taste). With Maddie's Secret, he directs his first independent feature film. The all-round artist steals the show himself as protagonist Maddie, a successful food influencer secretly battling a simmering eating disorder. For the film's script and style, Early drew inspiration from unadulterated 1950s melodramas (think Douglas Sirk), as well as those made for television in the 1980s, especially ones starring housewives in the lead role. The influence of John Waters, and even Showgirls, is never far away either. Played with total sincerity, the result is a hilarious satire that at the same time dares to be vulnerable.

Behind the lines, young soldier Pierre (Emmanuel Macchia in a striking debut) discovers an unexpected world of theatre, music and tenderness. At its heart is the charismatic Francis, played with irresistible flair by Valentin Campagne. The pair’s remarkable chemistry earned them the prestigious Best Actor award at Cannes. With Coward, Dhont gives his signature sensitivity a far broader canvas, allowing the classic war film to blossom into something unexpectedly sensual and tender.

films.title: Old Joy
intro: VIDEODROOM 2026 kicks off with an extraordinary cinematic experience. To mark the 20th anniversary of Kelly Reichardt’s Old Joy, we present a special screening of this melancholic indie masterpiece featuring a world-exclusive live score. For one night only, acclaimed harpist Mary Lattimore will transform the film’s atmosphere, replacing the original soundtrack with her ethereal and meditative harp compositions.
description: Old Joy follows two old friends—played by Daniel London and iconic singer-songwriter Will Oldham (aka Bonnie ‘Prince’ Billy)—who have drifted apart over the years, as they embark on a camping trip. Along the way, they drink beer, shoot at tin cans, and share long, meaningful silences. While little happens on the surface, a beautiful and poetic portrait of a strained friendship, broken dreams, and long-faded pasts unfolds between the lines.

With this bittersweet sketch, Reichardt placed herself at the forefront of American independent cinema, creating a film that resonates long after the final frame and continues to provoke reflection. Through renowned films such as Meek’s Cutoff and First Cow—always produced on limited budgets, filmed on location, and devoid of blockbuster stars—Reichardt has emerged as one of the most prominent American directors of the past two decades

For one night only, the original soundtrack of Old Joy by indie darlings Yo La Tengo will be tucked away, and replaced by the intimate sounds of Mary Lattimore. Since her 2013 debut The Redrawing Room, she has become a mainstay of the American experimental folk scene. Her impressive list of collaborators includes artists such as Kurt Vile, Meg Baird, Harold Budd, Thurston Moore, Sharon Van Etten, Jarvis Cocker, Steve Gunn, Julianna Barwick, and Fursaxa.

Her music shifts seamlessly from delicate and dreamy to complex and overwhelming. A virtuous musician, Lattimore masterfully juggles countless effect pedals live, yet can just as easily make her harp—stripped of all electronics—sing like no other.

imdb.plot: Two old pals reunite for a camping trip in Oregon's Cascade Mountains.

Intuitively and thoughtfully crafted, Jean is, on both sides of the camera, refreshingly honest. A coming-of-age documentary about a determined adolescent fighting for his chances. But is it a fair fight?
